#3789. Bethesda reportedly revealing The Elder Scrolls 6 next month, and we may know what its subtitle is going to be

Bethesda's hugely anticipated and long-awaited fantasy role-playing game The Elder Scrolls 6 could be revealed "as soon as next month", a new report has claimed - right in the midst of Microsoft's ongoing restructuring efforts.

Per The Verge, this new Elder Scrolls adventure carries the subtitle "Sentinel", which aligns with fan speculation, and the outlet corroborated prior reports that the game takes place within the Tamriel region of Hammerfell. The game reportedly touches on "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts".

If the game is revealed next month - presumably The Game Awards in early December is a good place for it - it would mark eight years after The Elder Scrolls 6's initial reveal trailer, and 15 years since the release of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim. So, it's certainly been a while, though it's worth noting that The Elder Scrolls: Online has operated all through this period, to give fantasy fans something to bide their time with.

Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, said she'd played the game in August on a trip to the Bethesda offices, all while a giant inflatable rat and a union protest took place outside. Indeed, this reveal would take place shortly after Bethesda suffered job cuts - as did many other Microsoft-owned studios - as part of Xbox's "reset".

Xbox has been keen to keep fans optimistic of its prospects during what is undoubtedly a challenging time for the business. Yesterday, Sharma said there was "more demand than consoles available" when addressing a 14 percent dip in Xbox hardware sales. Microsoft's latest 8-K filing - a mandated finance report publicly traded companies have to file to the SEC - states in plain terms that "Xbox hardware revenue decreased 29 percent driven by lower volume of consoles sold".

Sharma has also pointed to the record performances of Minecraft and World of Warcraft: Forever's open beta, and congratulated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for having its "most acclaimed release in more than a decade". But Xbox's first-party release Gears of War: E-Day reportedly only sold more than 400,000 copies across Xbox and PC, following its day-one Game Pass launch. Analysts speculate that its presence on the service potentially cut into its full-cost sales.

All the while, we're seeing studios decide to not sell their game on Xbox altogether due to the company's presence on the BDS boycott list. Earlier this month, Big Walk's developers declared the game would not come to Xbox because of Microsoft's ties with Israel. And last night, both Celeste and Towerfall were removed from Xbox for the same reason.

So it's safe to say that The Elder Scrolls 6, if it is revealed next month, will arrive into a very different world than the one it poked its head into almost a decade ago. Whether it can help Xbox turn things around: that's the question.

The composer for Celeste and Minecraft guides us through the games on her PC.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Lena Raine's formative gaming experience was playing Myst on a Mac Quadra 610, exploring Cyan Worlds' enigmatic island in parallel with her father: "We each had our own playthrough, so we were sending each other notes in the little journal that it came with," she says. "I still have the little book that we wrote in."

Raine always aspired to be a composer for video games, but she initially joined the industry as a games tester for Nintendo America, working several other testing jobs before being hired by ArenaNet as a game designer. While working on Guild Wars 2, Raine designed a bell-choir minigame for the MMO's Winter's Day Christmas update, including writing the music for it. "It was a bizarre first-step into game music," she says. "But that eventually led to at last some visibility for the other music I was writing."

After leaving ArenaNet, Raine wrote the soundtrack for 2018's Celeste, and spent several years composing music for Minecraft, including several of its most popular 'Disc' tracks like Pigstep, Creator, and Otherside. Raine is currently writing music for the early access volleyball RPG Beastieball, while also returning to game design with her own project ANOTHEREAL, an RPG with schmup-style combat. "I have been working on [it] basically since the pandemic," she says. "I'm trying to aim to have something released within the decade."

Raine took a break from her various projects to show me around the digital concert hall of her steam library. We discussed Deadlock, sorted her schmup collection, and took a trip down MMO memory lane.

The current game that I'm playing is Deadlock. I've been playing it for a while now, basically since it was pretty early in that beta, alpha, whatever phase. I play with my wife and some other friends that we've got.

I've been having a lot of fun with it. I've never been a MOBA person and I've never been a competitive shooter person either. Usually, I get tremendously frustrated with online competitive shooters because I'm not very good. I'm not great at those sorts of games.

But I love the style and the world that Valve has made for Deadlock. I love spooky occult stuff. I just love that entire vibe. A lot of my personal online characters are like demon girl aesthetics, and so I'm just like "This is a game for me".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I've been really committed to learning at least one character, so I've been focusing on Ivy, which is the gargoyle. She's awesome. She's from the first set of characters. I initially just laser-focussed on her. I was just like "Oh, she's really cool".

The Mermaid Mask. I was playing it on the Steam Machine, so technically it's still installed. But it's a single-player, linear story game, so I will probably uninstall it at some point to save space.

It's still installed because I finished it yesterday, or two days ago. But I really loved that game. I played the previous game—Tangle Tower—in the Detective Grimoire series, and they just have such a playful way of designing characters and presenting them. The voice acting is really good. The mysteries are fun and interesting to figure out as you're playing through it. It's a detective point-and-click adventure, gathering clues and talking to all the suspects.

There's just [a] ridiculous amount of items in the game that you can ask everyone about. And it's all just voice dialogue about all of them. I'm just such a completionist about it. I just sit in front of the TV and I've been listening to the characters talk about 30 different items for an hour.

The one that I really wanted to talk about is Final Fantasy 11, which is one of the first PC games that I got fully obsessed with when I was younger, at high school into college basically. It's got uninstalled and reinstalled over the years. But I have it installed. I've checked in on my character, who has been there since the initial release date … I played a little Tarutaru character and mostly was a red mage and monk.

The interesting piece of history with me and Final Fantasy 11 is that I initially imported it from Japan. It has since transferred over to English servers primarily. But when I initially started playing the game, it was not out in the US yet, and you had to import the game. You had to make a Japanese account with a Japanese address. But there were forums set up for people that wanted to import the game.

So I joined these forums, and these were people who also played like Phantasy Star Online on the Dreamcast, so we were all buzzing about this new game Final Fantasy 11. So there were instructions of like "here's translated screenshots of every single setup thing to do."

I had taken one year of Japanese in high school. So I knew enough to navigate a menu. I didn't know how to converse very well in Japanese, but I knew what the characters for like black mage, red mage, warrior, attack, level up, those sorts of things.

[But] the thing about Final Fantasy 11 is it was such a deeply social game, because to level up past a certain point you needed to join a party. You could not solo past a certain point. So people would group in in levelling parties, and unless I was playing with friends, I would be in a group of Japanese players that I was trying to communicate with, and it really depended on the sophistication of the conversation that was going on that I could blend in or out myself as speaking English.

The majority of friendships that I had was with the English-speaking community, and it's funny because a number of those people have gone on to have some pretty illustrious careers. One of the people that I played with was Maximilian Dood, who's a fairly well-to-do YouTuber now. Another friend that I played PSO and Final Fantasy with was Jason Oestreicher who worked for Giant Bomb for a while. So I have these weird industry connections from playing this import Final Fantasy game years ago.

The highest number of hours is Elden Ring at 282 hours. However, not on Steam, I looked this up also, Final Fantasy 14, I logged into my character and did the playtime conversion, and it's 1,308 hours.

I feel like I've talked a lot about Final Fantasy, [so] to talk a little bit about Elden Ring. I've played pretty much all of the Dark Souls games and mostly attempted to do co-op with them because my wife and I love to play the games together, and we always have a very rough experience when it comes to FromSoft online stuff, because it's very insistent on opening yourself up to adversity when you're playing together with friends.

But with Elden Ring, when that came out, this was right before we moved to Canada … [when] we were in this transit dead space where all our stuff is half-packed and we just need to find the right place. And so we were just calming our brains down by playing Elden Ring together.

That also includes the DLC up until the final boss, because the final boss of the DLC was too steep of a difficulty curve for the build that we were both running. This was also at the time the person that got famous for soloing Melania, they came back and they were Let Me Solo Them instead. And so my wife actually summoned that person, who beat the final boss for her. I was extremely jealous.

It's a tricky question for me because, with Steam existing as a service, it's very difficult to not uninstall something if you need to save space. But I was looking at what I did have installed and I saw a pattern, which is I basically leave all my favourite schmups installed.

I love going back to games like ZeroRanger, Adventures of Ten and Till, Deathsmiles, Mushihimesama, a number of classic and newer schmups that I love playing, because it's that kind of arcade experience [where] it never gets old. You can keep going back to it, keep improving on it. It's been good research also, because I'm working on a game that has schmup combat in it. But I'm making it because I have this experience with schmups of not being great at them.

A lot of times it has to do with the music too. A really good schmup soundtrack is basically an album.

This one's easy because I'm a composer and I work on the computer, so it's my music software. My DAW of choice right now is Bitwig Studio. It's by ex-developers of Ableton. They split off and made this new DAW called Bitwig that is like if you took a bunch of chains off Ableton in a way where you an rewire everything under the hood.

There's just a really open approach to how it's designed, where you can use basically every version of VST, which is instrument software, that's out there. You can use Clap, which is an open-source plugin format. It can open files from Ableton. It can open files and import the settings and metadata and stuff.

It's the one that has won me over. I've been using Ableton since working on Celeste, because used to use Cakewalk Sonar. The very first piece of music that I wrote for Celeste, I wrote in Cakewalk Sonar, and then I switched to Ableton after that … I literally can't open the first level of Celeste anymore, because it's in software I don't have installed anymore.

The very first [Minecraft update] I worked on was the revitalisation of the Nether, which was the underworld space, and I was pulling from a bunch of survival horror vibes, writing this scary music that was really unsettling, which is funny that that was the first … because the existing tracks that Daniel, C418, did was very calming, soothing.

What most people know my Minecraft music as is the three discs that I wrote, as opposed to the tons of other tracks that I wrote … it's funny because, for [Pigstep] too it was just the developers saying to me, "For discs, you just write whatever you want" because the initial discs were just tunes that C418 wrote that wasn't necessarily related to anything.

One of the throwaway ideas was "What would music the Piglins listen to sound like?" And so I was just like "Dubstep for pigs!" That was the prompt that I made for myself, and I just made a funny little tune and people just love it.

It's created a funny effect. I think at Mojang now, because they've since worked with a couple other composers—I feel like my tenure has expired. I had some fun there, but I want to focus on other projects—but they've worked with other composers since then. But the prompt I keep hearing is 'Oh, Pigstep was such a banger that they want more bangers.' I started something there. It's gonna keep on getting discs that are bangers.

Immaculate. I don't really believe in putting anything on my desktop. I have my wallpaper, and it's a cute piece of art, and if I have anything minimised, I look at the art, and I have a folder structure for everything else.

He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims.

#3785. There are currently "no other Assassin's Creed remakes actively in development", says Ubisoft

Yesterday, Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, and the publisher's comments included quite a big surprise: there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

"One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin’s Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft said in a statement on its website. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

This has come as a shock to some players because, back in 2024, Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot specifically mentioned that upcoming remakes - plural - were in active development across Ubisoft studios. "Firstly, players can be excited about some remakes, which will allow us to revisit some of the games we've created in the past and modernise them; there are worlds in some of our older Assassin's Creed games that are still extremely rich," Guillemot said.

Given the success of this year's Black Flag Resynced - which sold over 3.5 million copies and "exceeded annual expectations within its first 14 days" - it's interesting to hear Ubisoft move away from what clearly seemed a popular way of revisiting older games. But it's worth noting that although Ubisoft isn't currently working on remakes, that doesn't mean we won't get them at some point in the future.

"Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back," the company's statement continued. "That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted." That last bit, if you're unfamiliar, is a commonly-repeated motto amongst the Assassin Order.

If you're curious about what's next for the franchise, we've got a few ideas. First, there's 'Codename Invictus', which is billed as a "PvP multiplayer Assassin's Creed experience" being led by a team of For Honor veterans at Ubisoft Montreal. The title remains shrouded in mystery, and we've seen nothing of how the game will look or play yet.

Then there's Assassin's Creed Hexe, in development at Ubisoft Montreal. This game is touted as a "darker, narrative-driven" experience that appeared to be aiming for a 16th century European setting when it was announced back in 2022. It was originally believed to be targeting a 2026 release, but earlier this year, Ubisoft head of franchise Jean Guesdon explained the publisher is "taking the time to deliver on its ambitious vision, which means we'll be quiet for a little longer". Following this, a report emerged in August stating that Hexe is still at least a year away.

The Assassin's Creed series remains a pillar of Ubisoft's output, even if the publisher has been enduring a lot of change lately. Late last year, the leader of the Assassin's Creed franchise, Marc-Alexis Côté, left Ubisoft. This coincided with a reorganisation of the company and the creation of the Vantage Studios subsidiary, established by Ubisoft and Tencent, to oversee development of the French publisher's biggest franchises, which includes Assassin's Creed.

#3784. Fortnite lets you plunder free cosmetics from the item shop in new One Piece season, but only if you hit gold

The real treasure were the friends we made along the way, but I only say this because there's no chance I'll find one of those.

Fortnite‘s new Treasure Hunters season brings One Piece‘s pirate themes to the game, and starting today, the luckiest players can find the shooter’s biggest treasure: two weeks of free cosmetics from the item shop. Just make sure you’re digging in the right spot.

The Treasure Hunters season launched on Nov. 1, with Epic calling it “The Greatest Adventure of All Time” (I’m guessing the devs forgot about Outer Wilds). As part of the festivities, battle royale players can find special treasure chests loaded with loot.

One of the possible rewards in the chest is a Pirate Shop Token, which grants you and your team two weeks of free cosmetics in the item shop. This offer applies to most items puchased with V-Bucks, but transactions with real money are off the table. These can include the One Piece skins that arrived in the game with the collab on Nov. 1, plus whatever’s on tap during that time period.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

You can reportedly receive two different types of Pirate Shop Tokens: one lets you time your two weeks between November and Dec. 15 this year, while you can activate the other from Jan. 1 until the end of 2027.

Of course, this generous prize seems to have drastically low drop rates. You must first find the special treasure hunt chests, then luck out in getting the Pirate Shop Tokens from them. The announcement mentions “Mastery Mondays and Treasure Hours Sundays” throughout the season, which will include “boosted drops.” The post doesn’t officially specify if this affects Pirate Shop Tokens, however.

Fortnite is bringing the big guns this month, including a cosmetic-filled collab with One Piece. The items are spread out around the shop: Luffy, Nami, and Usopp anchored in the store alongside the season release, while Zoro, Sanji, and the Chopper Sidekick will arrive on Nov. 7.

With this being Fortnite, of course, there’s also a plethora of other skins up for grabs throughout the month—including A$AP Rocky, Lil Uzi Vert, Kasane Teto, and Cap’n Hatsune Miku. I’m not quite sure what the connecting thread is, but at least the One Piece skins seem cool.

The story surrounding 2014's Seth Rogen-fronted comedy, The Interview, remains one of the strangest and craziest stories in movie history. Rogen's edgy comedy -- which centers on a plot to killing North Korea’s president, Kim Jung Un -- created a major global incident. It was a massive problem for Columbia Pictures, and then-President Barack Obama had to address said film in regard to the protection of free speech. While I knew all that, I wasn't aware that Martin Scorsese ended up having one of his own projects squashed as a result.

Scorsese recently sat down with his daughter, Francesca Scorsese, to talk about his creative process, ideas he wants to explore and some of his biggest cinematic influences. During the interview. the director revealed that he actually planned on making a Cleopatra movie. However, after The Interview created chaos at the studio, Columbia (a subsidiary of Sony), they ended up dropping the project. He told Tribeca:

We were gonna do Cleopatra at one point, and then they made fun of [Kim Jong Un], and he got mad and blew up everybody at Columbia. …. He ruined Cleopatra.

This is such a major bummer, and a crazy way for a movie to get squashed. For more context, after The Interview was announced by Sony and given a release date, North Korea was upset about the implications of the film. It was the North Korean government's belief that the movie represented an act of terrorism and, in time, there were threats of violent retaliation if the film wasn’t pulled.

A month before Rogen and Evan Goldberg's movie came out, the now-infamous Sony hack occurred and thousands of confidential information and correspondence was leaked. The FBI concluded that North Korea intiated the attack, despite the country denying responsibility.

Based on what Martin Scorsese's comments, Sony may have been trying to do damage control after the hack, and Cleopatra was collateral damage. This truly is unfortunate, because it seems like the cameras were close to rolling on the historical epic. The Oscar winner said they even had a script worked out and a major actress was also attached:

We were gonna do it. Eric Roth was ready on the script. Angelina Jolie, we were going…. She was Cleopatra the seventh. It was going to be really wild.

The Shocking Connection Martin Scorsese, James Cameron And Paul Thomas Anderson's First Oscar Wins Share

I’m so saddened to hear this, given how cool the idea seems, and I would've loved to have seen this on the big screen. Scorsese only jokingly blamed Seth Rogen for the situation, though. At the end of the day, and I think Scorsese would agree, Rogen made a movie that was provocative, and it led to an extreme reaction. Later in the interview, Scorsese even mused that the issue stemmed from North Korea not having a sense of humor. Since the controversy went down Rogen has admitted to being traumatized by the situation, but ultimately, his country backed his right to free speech.

While Cleopatra didn't see the light of day, Scorsese went on to make incredible work instead of the biopic. He directed both Silence and The Irishman in the years that immediately followed, which may or may not have happened if he was busy with Cleopatra. Ultimately, it may have been for the best, and who knows, maybe another studio will revive that 2014 script in the future.

Martin Scorsese fans can check out his latest film, Killers of the Flower Moon, which is currently streaming with an Apple TV+ subscription. You can also now revisit the hoopla-causing comedy, The Interview, which is available to rent on Prime Video.

#3782. Final Fantasy 14 Evercold Gets A Month Long Delay But An Awesome New Trailer

DelayEvercoldFinal Fantasy XIVMMORPGTrailer

There was good and bad news at Final Fantasy XIV‘s Japan Fan Fest. The bad news was that the MMORPG’s new expansion Evercold has been delayed by about a month. Originally set for sometime in January, the full launch will now arrive on February 23, 2027. The good news is that Evercold now has its third and final teaser trailer, a six minute cinematic that sets up the narrative stakes for Final Fantasy XIV‘s biggest update in nearly three years.

“Tell me about the Promised Land,” a young girl asks early in the trailer. A wise old lady recalls a time of beauty and abundance that gave way to a “relentless ice” as magical beasts took over the mainland. People abandoned the continent for the skies above. The rest of the trailer is pretty much a ton of breathless views of massive city-sized airships (called Realmships) and cool battles showing off new job classes like the tanky Bastion who wields gunshields called Skyltborgs. Something that Square Enix doesn’t get enough credit for in its fantasy world building style is sneaking guns into stuff and making it look elegant and cool as hell.

The trailer also showed off the new DPS class called Zephyr, which wields a cross bow and a neat bird companion. It received its own breakout trailer giving fans a quick lowdown on how it will work. In fact, there were a lot of trailers to come out of the Japan Fan Fest. We got another teaser for the Neon Evangalion crossover event coming in 2027 as well as deep dives into the new locations and other changes coming with version 8.0 in Evercold. It will give players plenty to chew on as they wait a month longer for the full release.

Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 (there’s a trailer for the collector’s edition, too). Those who pay for the pre-order (any edition) will get early access to the expansion starting Friday, February 19, 2027. While a four week delay isn’t a big deal, this does mean that February is now even more packed. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, God of War Laufey, Persona 4 Revival, and Fable all come out within a week of Evercold‘s early access window. Should be fun!

#3781. Games industry honours beloved actor Sir Patrick Stewart, as the legendary Star Trek and X-Men actor passes away

"An emperor, a captain, and an inspiration to us all."

As I'm sure you're all now already aware, legendary British actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died, aged 86. His Instagram account announced the news yesterday, saying he died at home in Los Angeles surrounded by friends and family, following "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia".

Stewart, a poised and charming actor, was probably best known for his on-screen roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, and Charles Xavier-slash-Professor X in various X-Men films. But he also enjoyed a long and celebrated career on stage.

Stewart appeared in games, too, most notably in Bethesda's fourth Elder Scrolls game, Oblivion, as Emperor Uriel Septim 7th. He effectively kicked the adventure off, narrating the game's intro with gravitas before appearing as Septim to the player in their prison cell. There, he declared he'd seen the player in his dream and proceeded to let us free.

"I️ was born 87 years ago," Stewart's opening monologue began. "For 65 years I've ruled as Tamriel's emperor. But for all these years I've never been the ruler of my own dreams. I have seen the gates of Oblivion, beyond which no waking eye may see. Behold, in darkness a doom sweeps the land. This is the 27th of Last Seed, the year of Akatosh 433. These are the closing days of the Third Era, and the final hours of my life."

Bethesda, upon hearing of Stewart's passing, posted a picture of Emperor Uriel Septim from the recent Oblivion remaster, alongside the words: "Rest in peace to Sir Patrick Stewart - an emperor, a captain, and an inspiration to us all. Our thoughts are with his loved ones."

Stewart also notably voiced the narrator in both of MercurySteam's Castlevania: Lord of Shadows games, and appeared in a number of X-Men games and Star Trek games, as well as smaller projects like Polish Holocaust game My Memory of Us. In honour of his life and work, The Star Trek Online community gathered in large numbers, arranging spaceships in long lines to mark his passing.

Messages celebrating the person Stewart was have flooded social media overnight, written by the many people he impacted during his life and long career. Long-time X-Men collaborator and Wolverine actor Hugh Jackman said: "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

And Sir Ian McKellen, the Magneto actor who was considered one of Stewart's best friends, gave an overview of the many years the two had known each other, from being "ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago", to working on X-Men together. McKellen recalled cautioning Stewart about taking the lead role in Star Trek because of the effect it would have on his stage career - advice Stewart fortuitously overrode. McKellen referred to his friend as "the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic".

Rest in peace, Sir Patrick Stewart. There won't be another like you.

F-Stop was a result of a post-Orange Box, 2007 Valve game jam.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As reported by Kotaku, a near-mythical canceled Valve game called F-Stop has been reconstructed from material contained in separate leaks. Direct access to the build seems a little shaky at the moment, but full playthroughs of the game, like this one by Meme Man? on YouTube, are starting to pop up online.

Most of F-Stop's assets came out in this August's Steam "teraleak," but the final pieces⁠—F-Stop's source code and mapsrc data⁠—were only just acquired by the Valve Cut Content Team Discord, which appears to have gone private amid all the newfound attention over F-Stop. With the Discord currently invite-only, you gotta know a guy (or know a guy who knows a guy) to play it yourself.

The Half-Life Wiki has the skinny on F-Stop's origins in the "Directed Design Experiments." Following the megahit launch of the Orange Box in 2007, Gabe Newell effectively shut Valve down for a three-month game jam that produced five prototypes, F-Stop among them.

It applied Team Fortress 2's cel-shaded art style to a vision of Aperture Science in its prime, all mid-century wood-paneled office optimism. F-Stop's central mechanic was a camera that could capture objects in the world, then place them elsewhere to solve puzzles. The excellent 2023 game Viewfinder would apply a similar concept to a full commercial release.

But while loved internally at Valve, F-Stop's playtests were apparently more tepid. The game was shelved, though elements of its worldbuilding would appear in Portal 2 and Aperture Desk Job. It's fun to recognize some of these early ideas in the F-Stop longplays: From the jump, we get a version of Cave Johnson (sadly sans-J.K. Simmons in prototype) talking to the player, as well as the first instance of Aperture Personality Cores as companions in the puzzling.

Given F-Stop's "road not taken" nature, particularly compared to the megathit Left 4 Dead and Portal 2 that would follow, I don't really mourn the fact that we never got to play its final version. It is, however, extremely cool that the prototype game is now preserved for posterity.

#3778. Doom Director Says ‘We’re Doing Great’ After Half Of id Software Was Laid Off

Doom: The Dark AgesId SoftwareMachineGamesWolfenstein 3

Xbox’s summer reset hit a lot of storied game studios very hard. Among them was id Software, the long-running maker of the iconic Doom franchise. Roughly half the studio was canned just 24 hours before it launched its big expansion to Doom: The Dark Ages. Questions have swirled about the studio’s future and what it will still be capable of after deep cuts to important departments that scattered decades of combined institutional knowledge. According to studio co-director Marty Stratton, things are still going swimmingly.

“We’re doing great,” he reportedly told media at a press event earlier this week when asked about the impact of the layoffs, according to IGN. “Not to handwave the [layoffs] away…everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department.”

Big “My ‘incredibly viable studio’ T-shirt has people asking a lot of questions already answered by my shirt” energy.

One of the big asterisks for id Software coming out of the brutal Xbox reset was the long-term sustainability of id Tech, the proprietary game engine upon which the studio’s world class first-person shooters are built. “It is hard to make a game that is AAA thatâs like weâve done before with half the people,” Chris Hays, a veteran programmer at the company, said in August. “And by hard I mean impossible.â

Id Software has previously pushed back on those claims, arguing that the studio is about where it was when it was shipping Doom 2016 nearly a decade ago.Â MachineGames, which is working on the unannounced Wolfenstein 3, uses a different fork of id Tech for its projects. One suggestion has been that both studios could pool their remaining engineering sources to try to bridge the gap for future releases.

“We’re working more closely with MachineGames than ever,” Stratton reportedly told media this week. “We’ve always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we’re at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we’re really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We’d kicked this off earlier this year. We’re really excited about that. We’re both really really bullish on what we have ahead.”

Xbox has about a quarter of its “reset” left to go, with additional rounds of layoffs reportedly scheduled for November and January. It remains to be seen what Microsoft’s plans are for franchises like Doom in the future.

#3777. Sony has snapped up the film rights for Mouthwashing

Sony has snatched up the movie rights for Mouthwashing, the hit independent horror video game released in 2024.

Deadline reports Sony has obtained the rights from developer Wrong Organ and publisher Critical Reflex, and also brought on Karyn Kusama to direct the adaptation, a director perhaps best known for her work on the acclaimed Yellowjackets television show.

Sony has also enlisted Matt Manfredi and Phil Hay to write for the project, as well as production company Crooked Highway (who you may know for the Ethan Hawke–lead series of movies, The Black Phone). There is no word on which actors will star in the adaptation as of yet, nor whether the story will follow that of the game's own narrative.

Mouthwashing was a critically acclaimed release, and sold more than 500,000 copies as of February 2025. That was on PC alone, with the game made available on consoles yesterday.

This adaptation would arguably follow the path paved by the Iron Lung movie, created by Mark Fischbach (better known by his online alias Markiplier) and his own production company Markiplier Studios. That, a film adaptation of an indie horror game, performed exceptionally well at the box office bringing in $21m globally shortly after its premiere.

A Mouthwashing movie is an interesting idea. The main question is whether or not it would follow the plot and narrative structure of the game faithfully, or whether changes would be made to better suit the big screen. A sillier - but awfully tantalising - question, is who you'd like to see casted in the movie? Who'd play Swansea… Who'd play Jimmy?!? Questions abound.

#3776. GOG wants to bring back physical PC games, just like in the good old days—but the logistics are ‘very complicated’

The way they envision it would be perfect.

As reported by Games Radar, GOG would love to bring back physical PC discs, something that hasn’t been around for well over a decade now. Sure, collector’s editions and unique prints exist, but physical PC games are, put simply, a thing of the past. Digital stores dominate this side of gaming, and when we had 15 years of lightning-fast development bringing us huge and incredibly quick SSDs, as well as amazing internet connections, why wouldn’t they?

Steam is pretty much as good as a digital store can be regarding ownership and DRM-free copies. Things simply fell into place like a jigsaw puzzle, and so here we are with the vast majority of PC gamers not even owning disc drivers anymore. In spite of that, though, GOG remains committed to reigniting this lost art, with its senior business manager Marcin Paczynski saying it’s his “dream” to see it come to fruition.

“Ideally, my dream would be to be able to buy physical versions of those games on GOG. You go to your shelf on GOG, you click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario.”

In this case, you would actually get the best of both worlds: a digital copy, as well as a physical one if you want to REALLY keep it stored in a safe space. Keep in mind that GOG sells DRM-free copies only, meaning no publisher can take it away from you, nor do you need any underlying software to play these games, turning the disc into a sort of collectible if anything.

Creating a whole business based on this idea is “a very, very complicated thing,” Paczynski told Games Radar, not least because it’s “totally different from what we are currently doing.”

“Because we are talking about physical media, we need to think about logistics. We need to think about storage,” he said. Getting licensing deals and approvals from respective publishers is yet another hurdle to surmount, but the company remains very keen on the idea. “I really hope that at some point we will be able to do it. We’ll see,” Paczynski concluded.

Physical games are on their way out—not because no one wants them, but because publishers merely want to cut costs and save money on providing you the one service they have. We saw that even in the case of Sony, a company incredibly devoted to killing off not only physical games but perhaps even Blu-ray as a technology, its own first-party games had 30 percent of total sales be physical. Of course, Sony has to relinquish a 30-percent cut taken by retailers and must fund the production of boxes and, well, the printing of the discs themselves, which comes at a great overall cost at such a high volume.

So, physical media is very much beloved by the gaming world. But with everything being stupid expensive nowadays and corporations becoming greedier and greedier, it’s become excess fat that must be trimmed.

Despite Guillermo Rodriguez getting the lowest scores on Dancing with the Stars Season 35, he managed to stay around for quite a while. He and his partner Witney Carson made it to Super Bowl Night on the 2026 TV schedule, which was impressive. However, it sadly meant that the TV personality went home one week before Dedication Night. If he had made it that far, he would have dedicated his dance to his longtime co-worker and pal, Jimmy Kimmel. Now, he’s revealed some details about that dance (and I really wish we could have seen it).

In the week following Guillermo’s elimination from DWTS, he went on The Viall Files to speak about his experience on the show. He also discussed his love for Jimmy Kimmel, calling the talk show host “the best.” The host’s sidekick also explained that if he had made it to Dedication Night, he would have wanted to pay tribute to Kimmel by dancing to a song by one of his favorite musicians:

And about Dedication Night, I was like, yeah, you know what? If I pass next week, one of his favorite musicians is Huey Lewis and the News. I say, ‘Oh yeah, if we pass, we’re gonna dance tango, and we are going to dedicate it to Jimmy.’ And I told Witney, I say, ‘And we should dance to “The Power of Love”.’

Well, this is such a fantastic idea! And I’d love to see it. Not only would it have been a sweet song for Guillermo to dance to in honor of Jimmy Kimmel, but it’d also be fitting for the time of year. I note that because the song is famously used in Back to the Future, and Christopher Lloyd celebrated his 88th birthday on October 22 with a reference to both the movie and the Huey Lewis and the News song. So, all around, this would have been such a fun number to see on Dedication Night, which happened to air on October 20.

And who knows? Maybe we could still see it. Nick Viall, who hosts the podcast and was previously on Dancing with the Stars, told Guillermo he should still do the dance, just on an episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live. Listen, Whitney Leavitt did her freestyle on Call Her Daddy last year because she was eliminated before she could do it on DWTS. I think Guillermo could easily do the same thing on Kimmel’s show. Maybe he even could get Huey Lewis and the News to do a cameo, as Viall explained. It would seem Kimmel’s sidekick likes the idea, as he said:

Listen, I got to tell them that you told me that idea and everything, and hopefully we do it. And if we do it, we’re going to give you credit for that.

Well, they only have so much time to do this if they want to perform the number before Witney Carson gives birth and the show ends. However, I still think it’s possible. It sounds like a great idea, and one Kimmel would appreciate. Clearly, the host has a whole lotta love for Guillermo and was supportive of his DWTS journey, so I feel like he’d like something like this.

Guillermo went on to say that he felt bad when he got eliminated. However, Kimmel was in good spirits, as the man who has been his sidekick for over two decades recalled:

Jimmy, he said, ‘I’m proud of you. You did it. You did a good job. You make so many people happy. So many people were watching the show to see you and everything. And you just being yourself makes a lot of people great.’

That is so sweet, and it makes me want to see this “Power of Love” dance even more! And maybe it will happen on Jimmy Kimmel Live someday.

For now, though, you can stay up to date on Dancing with the Stars by making sure you watch Disney Night on Monday at 8 p.m. ET on ABC or with a Disney+ subscription.

#3774. The Outlast Trials Is An Exercise In Bad Taste And Good Politics

HalloweenHorrorSpooky Week 2026The Outlast Trials

In Rex Millerâs 1987 horror novel Slob, Chicago is under the blight of “Chaingang,” a 500-pound killer whose hunger for food and flesh is unequaled. Despite his appearance and more odorous stench, the walking death manages to maneuver with little detection due to what’s described as an uncanny charisma. He is effectively camouflaged. Such an unusual make of man, it turns out, is not born. Chaingang was designed by the Pentagon, part of a covert project to create an unstoppable murder machine to turn the tide in Vietnam. A Michael Myers for Uncle Sam.

The Outlast Trials is entirely consumed by this boomerang paradigm. In the co-op game, you and other lower rungs of society are subjected to mental conditioning tests. Solve puzzles, elude enemy detection and, occasionally, murder in unthinkable ways. A multiplayer prequel to Red Barrelâs hit 2013 survival horror OutlastÂ in which a citizen journalist discovers a creepy mental asylum providing cover for a backfiring supersoldier program, Trials is set in the late â50s, an era defined by Cold War paranoia. The game is set in the bowels of The Murkoff Corporation, a research firm tasked with creating sleeper cells.

With seemingly no limit on financing or bodies, the company is pushing the outer limits of narcotics and mind control. An elevated MK Ultra, Murkoff isn’t just designing the drugs a Charles Manson type might trip on; it’s drafting blueprints for its own BTK. Along with two or three friends, your compatibility will be tested in controlled environments, slaughterhouses recreating places of commerce, faith, bread and circuses. You will be asked to commit horrors. If you abstain, those horrors will be committed on you.

Recommended to me by author Grady Hendrix, Slob was published in the late â80s but soaked in the remnants of â60s counterculture, a lurid paperback made layered by its government paranoia. Tales of supersoldier programs are not unique. Half of all genre fiction seems to be about them and about half of those posit these programs as a bad thing. What makes it more interesting is that it has the clarity to paint the bigger picture, the fortitude to name the national projects that such mad science benefits, on whose behalf, and at what cost. It’s those key similarities that made me feel like Trials is influenced by Millerâs admittedly obscure work, and that make me far more confident the game took beats from the more popular, non-fiction 2019 tome Chaos by Tom O’Neill with Dan Piepenbring, which attempts to chronicle how many of these programs were real all along.

There is not a subtle bone in The Outlast Trials’ body. Each environment is saturated with blood. Where the heaps of mannequin parts end and the mountains of eviscerated limbs begin is indistinguishable. It is, quite possibly, the gnarliest game ever made, a truly inspired feat in an experience that may lead to heated debates over which “execution” is the most depraved. Due to their pacing and agonizing presentation, tarring, feathering and castrating a man dressed like Donald Duck can be as stomach-turning as pulverizing a judgeâs ankle bones with gavels. One trial implies that you, yes you, created the AIDS virus.

As you complete each trial, you must outmaneuver previous failed experiments whose augmentations, disfigurements, and madness make them incompatible with field work. Youâre also being pursued by the “prime assets,” singular all-star murderers whose reputation and charisma caught the attention of the Murkoff Corporation. This includes an oedipal Miami gangster, a leather cop with a lightning fetish, and conjoined twins who, despite their impossible disfigurements, converse like guests on William F. Buckleyâs Firing Line. Theyâre the Village People from hell. They are not just your enemies. They are enemies of life. Of dignity. Civil rights. Labor movements. Democracy. They are totems of empire enlisted on behalf of Murkoff, who are working on behalf of western interests.

In one of the gameâs endings, you awaken in the Congo at the far end of a firing line, sitting on your knees. Your interrogators demand to know the significance of a string of words, unknowingly speaking out your trigger phase. When you come to a second time, bodies have piled up and your thumbs are submerged in a manâs eye sockets.Â Previous endings follow a similar structure. You awaken in a Cuban hotel room, caked in blood. You come to in China, having freshly produced sexual blackmail. In the Saigon ending, youâre behind the wheel of a car, barreling past a checkpoint with a bomb strapped to your chest, mirroring real embassy bombings throughout the early ’50s. How this prequel will ultimately tie in with the incidents at Mount Massive Asylum feels less significant than how it will tie in with a larger alternative history. If Iâm allowed to trust my gut, I can think of one especially prominent political assassination that the game might be building up to.

This doesnât make the connective tissue to the other Outlasts insignificant, but the greater weight is less on the details than the inevitable arc. The Outlast Trials is about a weapons factory. Vampires and werewolves made on assembly lines and shipped overseas to violate political movements the powers that be deem inconvenient. To uphold American might. But inevitably, the violence returns. It returns to Mount Massive. It returns in lost boys and biker gangs. In summers of serial killers. In political assassinations carried out by individuals with holistically unplaceable values. It comes from an indifference to life, echoed from the top, festering all the way down. From the promise of stability being replaced with casino games. It is honed violence, intentionally manufactured for one purpose, but spilling over into oneâs backyard. It is a political project, but one that can only imagine itself on one end of the knife. And once it’s loose, look out behind you.

#3773. Forza director, who'd been with Turn 10 for 27 years leaves Microsoft, following studios merger with Playground Games

Dan Greenawalt, director, founder, and vice president at Turn 10 Games, has departed from the studio after spending 27 years as part of the company. This comes as Turn 10 is merged with Playground Games as part of Xbox's mass restructuring initiative that made headlines as it resulted in 3200 layoffs and four studio closures earlier this year.

In a report by The Verge, an internal memo written by Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams states: "Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft".

The memo continues: "It's hard to overstate Dan's impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original Xbox in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next.".

With Xbox's merger of Playground Games and Turn 10, the developers will be working in collaboration on the Forza and Fable franchises. The final track racer game that Playground Games developed prior to this merger was 2023's Forza Motorsport reboot, a wonderful racer that offered a sweet alternative to the more arcade Forza Horizon series. In Eurogamer's review, the game was described as: "A generous and lavish racer, with thrilling driving, that wants you for the long haul.".

"You click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I remember when I'd get bored as a kid, I'd marvel at the back covers of my older brother's PC game boxes—stuff like Guild Wars: Factions and the original World of Warcraft box, the inner cover of which showed a dwarf thwacking a yeti with that one epic sword that looked like a lightsaber. Even back then, the long switch to digital was underway, seemingly for good. But what if we could go back to the glory days of big, embossed boxes and girthy manuals?

That's the "dream" of GOG's senior business development and partnerships manager, Marcin Paczynski, as he recently told Gamesradar. Specifically, he wants to see a world where you "would be able to buy physical versions of [games] on GOG … You go to your shelf on GOG, you click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario."

I'm sure most PC gaming diehards would agree that, yes, an option to buy physical games—especially older games in a precarious state with regard to preservation—would be pretty neat. Even if you're the sort to snag DRM-free copies of everything you own, a disc makes a game easier to show off, keep close in the event that your hard drive explodes, or place in the seat across from you at a Michelin star restaurant.

The problem for GOG is that physical distribution is basically an entirely different business to running a digital storefront. "Because we are talking about physical media, we need to think about logistics, we need to think about storage," Paczynski said, adding that it's "a very, very complicated thing." But the idea has been on the company's collective mind "for years now," so he's not ruling it out.

If you don't want to wait, there's always projects like Big Box Collection that let you print your own facsimiles. Or buy used! A few scratches and a giant sticker reading "PROPERTY OF TREVOR" just lends character, right?

#3770. EA reportedly closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between Mass Effect 5 and Star Wars Battlefront 3

And it chose the "less risky, more predictable bet".

A new report has revealed that EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

The revelation comes from Bloomberg, which heard from "people familiar with the company's strategy" that the "recent emergence" of an opportunity to develop a third Battlefront game meant EA - a company saddled with $18bn in debt because of the recent leveraged buyout - would have two sci-fi projects, each likely to cost hundreds of millions of dollars to make.

It couldn't afford to make both of them so EA executives chose Star Wars Battlefront 3, because it was seen "as a less risky, more predictable bet than a new Mass Effect", Bloomberg reported - despite development for the game not even having begun yet.

An EA spokesperson said the company had "collectively reached this decision following months of planning, review, and analysis, including careful consideration of evolving business conditions, industry dynamics, and our long-term priorities". "While this is never easy," the spokesperson went on, "we ultimately have to make tough decisions to focus our teams on the biggest opportunities for our future, including investing in new projects across our portfolio."

The report highlights a few other contributing factors in EA's decision, including BioWare's unfavourable recent track record and a reorganisation of its executive ranks to include more EA Sports people, in favour of those advocating for BioWare. EA bosses even lamented Dragon Age: Veilguard's sales, suggesting it would have been better if the title was 'a live service game'.

Last week, following the announcement of BioWare's closure and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, an internal video for the project - known as Mass Effect Universe - was leaked, showing what appears to be a pre-rendered visualisation of it. The game was said to take place 600 years after the Reaper war, in the midst of a galactic cold war, and to have the player be "a cross between John Wick and James Bond" in terms of what they'd be capable of.

There was a promise of "Hitman-style freedom" in approaching levels, romance that "wasn't being sanitised", and for connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies. It's not clear how much work was done on it, but clearly a lot of planning had been done - far more, certainly, than has been done on Battlefront 3.

EA's Star Wars Battlefront 2 was released in 2017 and struggled, initially, to convince - partly because it was riddled with loot boxes. But years of adjustments and improvements left it in a much better place.

When Coraline came out back in 2009, it not only became one of the best stop-motion movies ever, but also the first of Laika films using the impressive medium. Since the studio’s latest movie, Wildwood, has been in the works for just as long as Coraline has been a movie, I love that they snuck in a bunch of easter eggs to pay tribute to what started it all for the studio. Let’s break down some of the ones I found out about when I scoured the internet.

First off is Coraline herself. Early in the movie, when Prue takes Mac on a fun ride through Portland, Oregon, a woman with blue hair and a yellow coat can be seen in the background, sitting under a tree. Check it out:

It’s a very brief easter egg, but it can be seen when Prue is passing a grassy park, and the shot goes to her smiling as she rides her bike. On Reddit, people also found a missing cat poster around town that looks very similar to the black cat in Coraline, too.

One scene in Wildwood I can’t wait to pause and look around in is at the beginning, when we're in Prue’s room. Her walls are filled with easter eggs! One that a lot of people have been noticing is that Coraline’s squid is on Prue’s shelf.

I don’t know if this one’s an Easter egg or not, but right below the squid is a little teddy bear that looks similar to Coraline’s own sleeping buddy. What do you think?

That one might be a stretch, but there are plenty more confirmed easter eggs to find in Prue’s room. Someone on Instagram confirmed there are also posters with Miss Spink and Miss Forcible and another one advertising Mr. Bobinsky’s circus mice. Also, if you look over to Prue’s laptop in the movie, apparently she’s actually watching the earlier movie there, too.

And, for the Kubo and the Two Strings fans, there's also a section of Prue's room with a poster with a beetle on it, strings of origami and a painting of a boat on it that's clearly referencing the Laika film.

One more that I definitely didn’t notice when I was watching, but saw in a video on Facebook pointing another one out: when Mac is kidnapped by a murder of crows, they are in a park, and one of the animal rockers is a chicken. This is a reference to Coraline because Other Mother famously uses chicken mitts. Plus, later in the movie, Other Wybie wears a chicken mask to rescue Coraline.

Thematically, it also makes sense for the chicken to show up here, because the chicken came up in Coraline when the character was being captured. In Wildwood it’s the scene where Mac is taken away, too.

I’m sure there are a ton more people will be finding as Wildwood continues to play in theaters. In the meantime, you can rewatch Coraline with a Disney+ subscription. I know I’ll be marathoning these movies in many upcoming spooky seasons to come. Also, check out our Wildwood interview to learn more about the amazing BTS about the film.

Anything can happen on Halloween. A dog can turn into a cat. Canada can eliminate daylight savings. Shigeru Miyamoto can drop a new holiday altogether. It doesnât hurt that in two weeks, the Nintendo Switch 2 edition of Pikmin 4 will drop. While the surprise Direct didnât provide any surprise new games, it did bring information on what the new edition will offer, plus an update on the mobile Pikmin Bloom.

Using the built-in microphone, the Switch 2 version of Pikmin 4 will allow you to command your pooch-like assistant Oatchi vocal instructions. Hopefully more dependably than what Hey You, Pikachu! could pull off. The new version will also feature an exclusive new mode, ‘Dandori Academy,’ a timed treasure rush. You will only get one try in this mode on Friday through Sunday, where your score will be submitted, but you will be allowed to practice and hone the trial through the upcoming week. As for Pikmin Bloom, the Pikminâs even tinier adventure, youâll soon be able to send your lil’ dudes underground. Caves are being added to the mobile game. Akin to the gauntlets of the console series, these caves promise heaps of treasure at the risk of total Pikmin devastation. The direct ended on a new animated Pikmin short, adding that the once mysterious cartoons will soon be a monthly occurrence. Miyamoto also introduced actress and Pikmin ambassador Fuka Koshiba, who caught his eye crocheting hats.

Happy Pikmin Day eve, everyone. I hope you are doing well.

#3767. BLEACH Mirrors High character tier list

Fulfilling every fan’s dream, BLEACH Mirrors High lets you join forces with some of Tite Kubo’s most iconic characters in an original storyline taking place after the series’ Thousand-Year Blood War.

But the game is also a gacha, where understanding which characters excel can be key, especially when pondering a reroll or investing in the right backups. Here’s our latest BLEACH Mirrors High tier list.

We divided our list into four tiers, from S to C, and selected the three-star versions of all characters as our baseline for evaluation while taking all of their Limit Break passives into account. Due to their customizable nature, the protagonist was not included.

True to what any fan can imagine, Ichigo and Aizen are the staple S-Tiers of Mirrors High and the game’s best Combo picks. Rukia and Rangiku then shine as its best Chain supports, with the latter being by far the best partner for Hitsugaya.

Although unable to perform at the same level as the above, those in the A-Tier can be just as destructive when under the right conditions or compositions. True to that, many of them are excellent wild card picks or secondary DPSs.

The B-Tier houses characters who are either unable to compete with the above or lack overall deck variety/kit versatility. This does not mean they cannot excel, just that their utility and ceiling will be limited by the opposition.

#3766. Crimson Desert Enhanced Edition gets a surprise demo on PlayStation and Xbox, lets you play for 5 hours and carry over your save data

Crimson Desert is one of 2026's most successful releases. The game managed to sell over 6 million copies in just three months, and ended up being so profitable that its publisher ended up giving each employee at development studio Pearl Abyss a $3,400 bonus. Since launch, the dev has been committed to improving the game and correcting some of the more egregious issues that were present at launch.

Now, over half a year after its launch - and with the publisher's revenue up a massive 419 percent - it seems the company is eager to let anyone that hasn't yet purchased the game try it out, completely free. To celebrate the launch of the delayed Charting the Unknown DLC, which came out yesterday, Pearl Abyss has made the first five hours of the game completely free to play for (nearly) anyone on Xbox or PlayStation.

Any trial progress you make carries over to the full game if you decide to purchase it, and once your five hours are up, that's it - you can't restart the trial on a different save or something like that. The timer is final.

Charting the Unknown is the first bit of DLC for the game - there's likely more to come - and a Switch 2 version of the sandbox fantasy RPG is currently in development. The developer has hinted at multiplayer-focused DLC in the future, as well as a sequel to the popular game. If you're curious what took the world by storm earlier this year, you can try the free trial on your console of choice right now.

Has anyone in Hollywood seen a bigger and quicker rise to fame this year than Obsession’s Inde Navarrette? I sincerely don’t think so. The 25-year-old not only starred in one of the best 2026 movies, but she’s also been cast in the MCU, is the latest SNL host and is now heavily predicted to be an Oscar nominee this awards season. Amid all that, she just talked about how she’s coping with her sudden fame, and her name-dropping Twilight is so relatable to me.

When the things around me are full of uncertainty and change, I often go back to familiar movies and TV I love. And that’s exactly what Navarrette is doing. In her words:

Sometimes you rekindle with yourself, you kind of do things that you loved when you were 7. And I recently have nonstop been watching Twilight ... So I’m going back to things that used to excite me, and that’s kind of how I’m using everything to unwind. A good shower. I took off my eyebrows. I’m trying different things to have fun and just also bring my feet back down to the ground.

Absolutely. I know exactly what she’s talking about. There’s something so cozy and rewatchable about the Twilight movies, and I constantly find myself returning to them all the time. There’s something about them coming into my life at a very pivotal time in my upbringing that makes it so when I turn it on, it calms me down, and always brings me joy.

From what we’ve heard about fame from other celebrities, it really has a dark power to change one’s life in potentially negative ways. But Navarrette sounds like she’s putting energy into remaining rooted in herself.

In the interview with People, she also said she spent most of the summer with her longtime friends going to the beach and playing pool at the “same dive bar.” She said they did “the same thing over and over again.” I imagine that was comforting for the star as she continues to catapult in popularity to the height of even being a meme and a Halloween costume.

After Navarrette hosts SNL, she has a long awards season campaign going with Obsession. The movie is campaigning for her to get Best Actress, along with Michael Johnston for Best Actor, and Curry Barker for Best Director, Best Original Screenplay and Best Film Editing. We also expect she’ll be filming her role as Rogue in the new X-Men movie next year ahead of its release date on May 5, 2028. She’s got a movie with Apple called The Waffle House Index, too, and has already filmed a thriller called Invertigo.

If you’re looking to rewatch the Twilight movies as Navarrette has just in time for hoa-hoa season, they are currently all available to stream with a Netflix subscription.

#3763. Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3's online servers are temporarily going dark, FromSoftware announces

Things might get even darker over in the world of Lordran without those silly, only sometimes helpful notes left by other players. Developer FromSoftware has announced that it's temporarily closing Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 servers because of an unspecified issue.

"Due to a server issue, the game servers for the following titles will be temporarily unavailable on all platforms," the RPG studio tweeted earlier today, before naming Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3.

While the server shutdown won't last forever, FromSoftware hasn't told series fans when exactly they can expect online play to be restored. That presumably means PvP invasions, summon signs and in-game messages that try to troll you off a cliff are unavailable for the time being.

"We will provide updates once we have information regarding the server restoration time. We apologize for the inconvenience," the studio added. I hope you've stocked up on Estus Flasks, at least.

Of course, this isn't the first time the Dark Souls trilogy has had to contend with server problems. In 2022, Bandai Namco took servers for all three Dark Souls games offline due to a security vulnerability affecting Dark Souls 3. The threequel went dark once again a few months later.

FromSoftware's next game The Duskbloods - the one with the jetpacks and vampires and a cute bird thing - hasn't been any luckier, either. The multiplayer-focused game's first network test had to be taken offline early due to similarly vague "server issues". More recently, FromSoftware delayed its Switch 2 exclusive into next year.

"While development of The Duskbloods is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027," the developer tweeted this week. "We apologise to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support."

#3762. A movie theater plans to hypnotize us into rewatching favorite movies for the first time—but I would just use it for Witcher 3

Hypnosis. Fact or fiction? Who knows. Some claim it works wonders, forcing them to quit habits they’ve had for decades or to pick up things they always wanted to do but never could. Others say it’s complete hogwash—a snake oil sale reliant on placebo and your own convictions.

Whether it’s true, I don’t know, but a movie theater seems to believe in its powers to the point of wanting to hypnotize viewers into forgetting their favorite movie.

The reason? You get to watch it for the very first time—again. As reported by Dexerto, a Dutch cinema chain called Pathé is hosting an experimental project called REWIND, which would theoretically allow viewers to mind-wipe and memory-hole their favorite movies and then experience them as if they had never seen them before. The project is taking up 30 moviegoers and kickstarting on Nov. 9 at its Buitenhof venue in The Hague.

It seems to work by bringing people into a session with a hypnotherapist—in this case, Victor Kraemer who apparently has decades of hypnotic experience under his belt—who would then, well, hypnotize you into forgetting. However, Pathé seems to maintain the procedure isn’t 100 percent certain, since it is unclear whether hypnosis can actually make you forget an entire movie. I’m positive it’s even more difficult if you’ve seen the thing dozens of times, as many do with their favorites.

If it does work, however, I would love to memory-hole The Witcher 3 from my mind and get to play that masterpiece for the first time again. In 2015, I had a HD 6670 and a dualcore Pentium G2030 supported by six gigs of DDR3 memory, running TW3 at a 12-15 FPS average. It was a horrible experience overall, but even as such, it became my favorite game of all time, to the point where my family invested a lot in a new machine that I bought the year after just so I could play TW3 on high graphics and a great FPS.

The story was just so gripping, so enticing, enthralling even that no amount of poor performance or lag or slow-motion could deter me from playing through it. Between 2015 and 2016 I probably put in over 300 hours in the game on that original hardware, and have come back to replay it time and again over the last 11 years. Blood and Wine is especially close to me, and I can’t even remember (pun intended) how many times I had seen that TW3 trailer with Orianna in it.

It’s the perfect game in almost every way, and I envy those who are yet to try it.

Grand Theft Auto's radio stations have long stood as an integral part of the series' whole vibe—either offering time capsules of the times each game was set in (Vice City), or offering a realistic blend of classic and modernity a la Grand Theft Auto 5's excellent music curation.

Welcome to Critical Hit, where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.

I've been just a tad giddy to discover what awaits me in Grand Theft Auto 6's car stereos when the game launches on November 19, which has me surprised that Rockstar teasing six of its upcoming stations earlier this month completely flew under my radar.

Well, now I've had a gander and listened to all 12 minutes of its DJs bantering and a peppering of bangers between. And I gotta say, I'm already jazzed to speed down Leonida's highways with some of these stations at full volume.

Rockstar's licensed music curation rarely misses, and that very much seems to be the continuing trend with Grand Theft Auto 6. While we don't know just how many radio stations there are in total yet—this is the first game where we'll be able to tune in to both terrestrial music stations and podcasts, it being 2026 and all—but the six that were teased were the exact kind of flavours I've come to expect from the series.

There's Latin station Cocoteo FM, classic country Back Country Radio, African channel AfroBANK FM, all-out metal hub The Chamber 106.6, pop banger central Flash FM, and hip-hop destination Dirty South Classics. I'm already 100% here for The Chamber's setlist, being an elder emo and all, with bands like Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer making their way onto Leonida's airwaves. But I'm also jazzed to see newer blood on the scene, like Bad Bunny's appearance on Cocoteo.

My biggest interest was in Flash FM, though. Non-Stop Pop has become such an iconic radio station for me, thanks to some excellent song choices and Cara Delevigne's delightfully deadpan delivery. It doesn't seem like I'm going to be disappointed, though—Alex Consani takes up the mantle as model-turned-radio-host alongside the excellent artist Robyn (of Bulletproof fame), and hearing one of my favourite songs in MGMT's Electric Feel is all the confidence I need in Rockstar's keen ear.

While the previews do show criminally little interactions between the hosts (it seems like Grand Theft Auto 6 is going for duos across all its stations, presumably for some easy back-and-forth banter), I'm sure there'll still be satire in droves to come.

#3760. Why Netflix’s Matthew Perry Doc Doesn’t Use Voiceover From His Memoir Audiobook, Per The Director

The filmmaker's rationale makes a lot of sense.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's been over three years since Matthew Perry died at 54 due to acute ketamine use and accidental drowning. Now, his loved ones are telling his story in a three-episode docuseries, The One About Matthew Perry, that recently arrived on Netflix as part of the streaming schedule. The production's director, Mary Robertson, has been discussing her approach to the doc, and she recently explained why she chose not to incorporate any of Perry's voiceover from the audiobook of his memoir.

The year before Perry died, he released his memoir, Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing. With the book, Perry didn't sugarcoat anything regarding his career and lengthy struggles with addiction and alcoholism. His text served as a jumping-off point for Robertson when it came to her making the doc. She also could've easily inserted snippets of Perry's narration from the memoir's audiobook to help her series. However, as Robertson told Variety, she wanted to shift the perspective a bit. She explained:

We wanted to craft a text that enriched what Matthew delivered through the memoir. His memoir delivers something that, by definition, is first person, and doesn’t include the accounts of those who can describe what it was like to love someone who is completely brilliant and generous and loving, but also grappling with this enormous monster that he carried on his shoulder for most of his life. This is their account that’s missing from the memoir.

Robertson makes an excellent point. The goal of The One About Matthew Perry is to tell the late star's story from the perspectives of those lucky enough to have known him. Perry was already fortunate enough to tell his story in his own words so, for Robertson, this was an opportunity to provide an alternate view of the content Perry so candidly laid out in his book.

A major element of the Netflix docuseries is the series of conversations conducted with Perry’s sister, Mia Perry Bowick. During a recent interview, Perry Wowick said what she loved about Robertson’s project was being able to hear her brother’s point of view of the same stories shared by others. To that point, Robertson said she loved Bowick’s interviews for the series and that she came from a place of “real intimacy and connection” to the man famous for his role on Friends.

The doc features stories from Perry’s closest friends, Roger Castillo and David Pressman, as well as former NBC president Warren Littlefield among others. Fans, however, won’t see Perry's Friends castmates in the docuseries. An insider said there was “no way” Perry's friend and co-star Jennifer Aniston. would agree to join the doc due to alleging wanting to avoid reliving her grief. The sitcom stars are still mentioned in the doc, of course, and their presence at Perry's funeral is even discussed.

Even though we won’t hear Matthew Perry’s memoir audiobook voiceover narration, it doesn’t mean his presence isn't felt in some sense in the docuseries. Mary Robertson included rare footage from a 2009 interview he did in the YouTube series Kevin Pollack’s Chat Show, where he narrated his own story five years after Friends ended. What Robertson seemed to want was a nuanced doc that was different from its subjects memoir, and overall, it seems she succeeded in making that.

Check out The One About Matthew Perry using a Netflix subscription now. You can also see his incredible work as Chandler Bing on Friends by streaming all 10 seasons with an HBO Max subscription.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#3759. Blizzard hints at console ports for World of Warcraft: Forever - "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want"

After more than two decades dominating the PC MMO battlefield, it sounds like Blizzard Entertainment's taking the idea of a World of Warcraft console port more seriously than ever.

World of Warcraft: Forever's beta seems to have been immensely popular with fans of the series. It's a brand new third version of the iconic multiplayer game that sits alongside WoW's Classic and Retail portions, and it's recaptured many a lapsed Warcraft sicko with tons of good changes, big and small - one of which is controller support for the first time ever.

Speaking to GamesRadar about the decision to keep World of Warcraft: Forever exclusive to PC players, despite now supporting gamepads, vice president and executive producer Holly Longdale hinted that the fantasy game might just make its way to even more devices and players over time.

"What you just described is really what we're after," she told the outlet. "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start."

Longdale reckons all gaming platforms might become "more ubiquitous" in the future, as well. She specifically named the Xbox Project Helix, which is said to be a PC-console hybrid device of some kind. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed the next-gen console can even play your PC games earlier in the year.

"Honestly, we just want to be able to play it anywhere. We've seen people getting it working on the ROG Ally X," Longdale added. "I think just doing some of the work we're doing on gamepad is going to give players a lot of flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles."

World of Warcraft: Forever properly launches on the 4th of November.

Despite struggles in the rest of the Xbox division, Forever's beta was supposedly the "largest" in series history. Elsewhere, Longdale acknowledged that some of the developer's decisions won't make everybody equally happy: "I think the lesson we learned the most over time is 'You don't listen to the loudest people in the room.'"
