#3758. Going Back To Kingdom Hearts’ Tarzan Level Is About To Make Me Crash Out

All right, weâre one month into Guiding Key, Kotakuâs year-long Kingdom Hearts replay, and that means itâs time for our one-month check-in! For years Iâve heard people say that the first Kingdom Hearts has aged poorly and you should just skip it. âNonsense,â I thought. There wasnât a chance in hell that I would skip the original adventures of Sora, Donald, and Goofy. That game is so special to me, surely my love for some of its iconic moments would give me the nudge I needed to overcome Square Enixâs nearly 25-year-old jank and awkwardness, right?Â

Admittedly, Iâve been having trouble getting through Kingdom Hearts due to various unrelated circumstances (I moved apartments this month and also BioWare was shut down so Iâve been very busy in my daily duties here at Kotaku), but also, every time Iâve opened the game Iâve been met with some crazy flimsiness that I guess I just didnât know enough at the time to recognize as the serious flaws they are.

Kingdom Hearts wants to be a lot of things, and itâs certainly pretty ambitious for a 2002 PS2 game. But Square wasnât one to play it safe, so that wouldâve been par for the course. Itâs an action game, an RPG, a space flight combat sim, and, perhaps most regrettably, a platformer.

Soraâs notoriously floaty jump has been the bane of my existence in this replay. Trying to get this boyâs big-ass shoes to land where I want them to has been particularly difficult in its finicky recreations of Disney worlds, and nothing quite captures that like the Tarzan world called Deep Jungle. Sora and friends move through this world by jumping, swinging, and even grinding on the jungleâs various plants and platforms. In many platformers, the challenges are made less frustrating by the fact that youâre offered an immediate redo when you fall from your intended path. Deep Jungle, however, has layers to its map such that, if you fall from one, youâll go down to the other, which means that every time you fall from a vine or miss a landing, youâre falling down to another level, and getting back up to where you were is tedious as all shit. Hereâs a clip from friend of the site Jesse Vitelli that illustrates it all pretty well.

In general, movement has been one of my biggest issues with this game during my replay. Like yeah, itâs dated, but the PS2 era had a lot of really tight and snappy action games. In Kingdom Hearts, however, Soraâs floatiness makes any jump feel like a risk, which frustrated me to the degree that at one point I had to put my Switch 2 down and go play Overwatch to be mad at something else.

On a more positive side, what has stuck out to me in these early worlds is just how much Square Enix was clearly allowed to play with the Disney source material in cool ways, even though they definitely feel smaller than I remembered them being. Wonderland is dramatically smaller than I recalled, which isnât too much of a bummer because it doesnât move me as much as the other two early Disney worlds. Despite my grievances with the running and jumping of it all, Deep Jungle, with its portrayal of Tarzan villain Clayton as basically Just a Guy controlling Heartless is one of the earliest moments of Square Enixâs dark fantasy perfectly blending into a Disney world when one might think them entirely incongruous.

The standout in this early batch of Disney worlds, however, is far and away the Olympus Coliseum. What it lacks in scope, it makes up for in being one of the most intriguing marriages of Disney and Final Fantasy that Square pulls off early on. Though there are literally only three âroomsâ in this world, Square does a lot with the Hercules setting with very little. What could easily have been just a glorified stage for challenges and boss fights instead sets up some of the most intriguing crossovers in the game. Cloud Strife, the brooding hero of Final Fantasy VII, is also here to take part in Philâs games, specifically to kill Hercules on behalf of Hades. As a result, you have to fight him, and he is one of the toughest fights in the game thus far. His bandaged Buster Sword, swift strikes, and superior mobility had me on my toes the entire time. Donald and Goofy were practically dead weight as they were quickly taken out, but I finally beat him with no potions left in my pocket. The fight against Cerberus was definitely more predictable, but it lived up to Cloudâs.Â

Overall, Kingdom Hearts has been more fun to dissect than to actually replay, which is in keeping with what Iâve heard people say whoâd gone back to it more recently than I had. By god, I hope the earnestness can carry me through because this clunky-ass shit is grating. But enough about me, letâs check in with yâall!

From what [the developers have] said recently, this is kind of the case, that [early Final Fantasy cameos in the series] were pretty much placeholders or something to that effect. I do think it’s a bit overstated how much of a crossover it is between Disney and FF when in reality it’s Disney through an SE lens with some FF cameos (even since the first game, there hasn’t been a single FF world and Disney characters vastly outnumbered FF characters)… BUT FF (or other SE cameos like TWEWY) have been fun and I miss them. They don’t need to be as central as the Traverse Town gang in KHI but they could still make a cameo. â Enfy, on the nature of Final Fantasy cameos in Kingdom Hearts.

But they were more than a cameo. I understand they didn’t directly affect the story, but they did help to give that game its uniqueness and added the fantasy feeling of the game. Once they took out the Sephiroth fight in part 3 and just made it into Disney advertising, that’s when I quit.Â

Tell me a single original boss fight in KH3 that was better than fighting Sephiroth.Â  We need Final Fantasy back in the series. â shin dean, advocating for a return to Final Fantasy characters

Hey now. The Gullwings are great. â Amethyst, regarding the Final Fantasy X-2 characters as they appear in Kingdom Hearts II.

This will likely be its own blog when we get to Kingdom Hearts II, but I genuinely couldnât stand what they did to Yuna, Rikku, and Paine in that game by turning them into tiny pixies instead of letting them appear alongside the other Final Fantasy characters. Yuna, in particular, is my favorite character in all of Final Fantasy so that stung. But I wonât go too deep into that here. Weâre not even at that game yet! â KS

The segments just took too long, in my opinion. If Kingdom Hearts were made today, I can almost guarantee there’d be an option to skip the Gummi Ship sections entirely. They’d be relegated to more of an optional side thing that you aren’t forced to do. â StealthMantis on Kingdom Heartsâ Gummi Ship segments

Why is everyone building their gummi ship to look symmetrical? I’m proud that I made my ship look like hieroglyphs on acid. â shin dean on custom Gummi Ship designs

In college I visited a friend whose roommate was playing the first game and was on a ship level – that ship was my intro to kingdom hearts and probably why Iâve never played a single game in the series thus far! â Jeffrey Gilbert on the Gummi Ship segments

My enjoyment of these segments went up when I realised that I could just make a giant ship with a colossal HP pool and just Kool-Aid Man through it all. â Joesph Lillo on Gummi Ship segments

I spent hours building Gummi ships bc I enjoyed the builder. I tested most of those ships. The actual on-rails stuff was fine but I can see how it would be an annoyance to anyone that it doesnât vibe with. â Steve Jones on Gummi Ship building

Back in the day I really enjoyed building Gummi ships. In my recent playthrough I kind of just couldn’t be bothered to do anything with building ships other than slapping whatever weapons and engines were strongest on there and yeah it’s definitely very boring. The only real value is the lego spaceship building.

I know I’m getting ahead of myself but every aspect of it was an improvement in 2. Better building, more vibrant and dynamic levels, and even more skippable than the original if you weren’t a fan. In the 3rd game, ship design was arguably even better, but I felt like the open world didn’t have anywhere near the personality of the routes in 2 (and then was a big slog if you didn’t want to bother).

In my recent playthrough of 1 I was reminded of the ability of the ships to transform and it’s a shame it never came back because that was the game that needed it least. â Envy on Gummi Ship segments

They were also pointless in the fact that I believe you can just hold X to shoot straight and never actually have to move or aim, and youâll get through the levels to the next world just fine, with enough health to survive. â Bobman32x on Gummi Ship segments

I liked it. I built all sorts of ships. It was fun for me. Kinda wish I was smarter and transferred that fondness to real-world aircraft building. â Jason Douglas on Gummi Ships

Yes. It’s dumb, mindless, and one of the biggest eyesores on the system. â Batista Thumbs Up on Gummi Ship

Melvor Idle 2 has gained a subtitle: A RuneScape Adventure.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's easy to knock old-school RPGs, especially grindfests like RuneScape, for being games where you endlessly and sometimes mindlessly make numbers go up. But Melvor Idle, which self-bills as a RuneScape-inspired idle adventure game that claims to squeeze the genre into its "purest form," leans into that—and Jagex has partnered with developer Games by Malcs to make the RuneScape connection official.

The announcement blog from Jagex reads, "Melvor Idle takes a lot of inspiration from RuneScape and you can just feel it," adding that Jagex's support (and branding) is intended to help make the game "even bigger … while Melvor Idle 2 doesn’t take place in Gielinor, we think a fan-built idle game inspired by our MMOs is more than worthy of the title."

This isn't the first time Jagex has collaborated with Games by Malcs. It became the first Melvor Idle's publisher five years ago, albeit without a branding tweak. While RuneScape has had its fair share of monetization controversies over the years (you can see just how skeptical people were of the partnership when it was first announced on Reddit), it doesn't seem like Melvor has been compromised by trouble along those lines—the announcement blog proudly proclaims the sequel will have "no microtransactions."

Beyond that, it seems like a bigger version of the familiar idle RPG with overhauled visuals and a higher level cap of 120. You might find it a bit odd that it's a "RuneScape Adventure" that doesn't take place in the MMO's setting, but I'm not sure how many people are really invested in Jagex's games for the scintillating lore and worldbuilding. If you end up feeling like a stranger in a strange land, you can always hire someone to spam "buying gf" in a chat window while you get your idle on.

#3755. GOTY hopeful Mina the Hollower bought the studio financial stability "for now," while the Shovel Knight devs work on a new 3D game

Yacht Club Games has confirmed that most of its developers are now working on a brand new 3D game (potentially Shovel Knight 3D), after the critically-acclaimed Mina the Hollower did well enough for the team to continue.

Before launching its old-school adventure game earlier this year, Yacht Club described Mina the Hollower as a "make-or-break" moment for the beloved indie studio. A global pandemic and a failed experiment to turn Yacht Club into a multi-project studio had left the developer on thin ice, it seems.

But Mina the Hollower sold well enough to buy the studio more time, according to a new Reddit AMA full of interesting tidbits. Asked if Mina was able to secure financial stability for the company, Sean Velasco simply said "yes… for now!" Mina managed to sell over 500,000 copies in its first two weeks, so it's well on its way to the one million copies the devs were once hoping for.

For the foreseeable future, the devs aren't ready to talk about the kinds of DLC and spin-offs and follow-ups that dear old Shovel Knight enjoyed for many years, but they're not abandoning their newest baby either. "We're working on more post-release features," the devs wrote, which includes "expanded randomizer options, enemy and boss randomization, more modifiers, speedrunner features" and more ways "to do even more in Mina."

Another fan also asked the folks at Yacht Club about their unannounced 3D Shovel Knight game - Velasco previously told Bloomberg that the game was halfway done before the entire studio put all hands on deck for Mina, and pivoted back into a one-game outfit. Alec Faulkner stopped short of confirming Shovel Knight 3D, but said "most of us are currently working on a 3D game, yes!" Alright then, Alec, keep your secrets. "Not sayin more! Other than that it’s gonna be soooooooo awesome."

Co-founder Nick Wozniac went further into the state of the developer, and why splitting the team in half was probably a mistake. Here's what he had to say on the matter: "Sales are the things that keep the company afloat so it's not born from greed (mostly) that we say we'd love to see more sales, it's all about continuing to work together and make great games and reaping the rewards along the way. We are doing ok and learned a lot this cycle. I think we learned mostly that keeping the team tight and focused is what helped Mina land. Splitting the team up to work on two games was something we could have corrected a long time ago but I'm glad to be where we are now. Just gotta pocket those lessons and use them to drive you forward."

Eurogamer's five-star Mina the Hollower review called it an "adventure that takes inspiration from the greats."

Jane Lynch’s Weakest Link has been one of the best game shows on TV in recent years, and I’ve been tuning in every week this season for the Celebrity Weakest Link edition. The more star-studded version of the show is relatively new, as it’s only been on the TV schedule since last year, but it’s reliably a fun thing to turn on Mondays. However, something has been getting on my nerves as of late.

The premise of Celebrity Weakest Link is super straightforward. A bunch of celebrities get together to answer trivia questions in hopes of winning a bunch of money for the charity of their choice. After every round, the celebs have to vote one of the contestants out until the strongest link among them is left standing.

There’s always a theme, which I’ve been loving. The “Reality Villains” episode had me unexpectedly rooting for Tom Sandoval and the “8 Degrees of Jane” episode got me in my feelings over Glee. Though, I’m noticing one thing about the format that irks me. Whenever there’s a tie in the votes (which inevitably happens every episode), it’s super anticlimactic.

In the show, when there’s a tie for the weakest link that round, the strongest link gets to pick whether to vote out the person they voted for and pick the other most popular option. I’ve literally never seen the strongest link choose an option other than who they originally voted for. So, after watching for a while, it just feels like a pretty lame aspect of the show that serves no purpose but to eat up some time. After seeing so many episodes, it’s got me booing at the screen.

Look, I get it, a game show like Celebrity Weakest Link thrives on being dependable, light and fun rather than volatile, but I think the tie thing really flattens out the otherwise great flow of it. I think it’d be kind of fun if the strongest link had to briefly interview the two celebs in contention to make their decision. You know, make the two on the chopping block plead their case somehow after getting certain questions wrong. Another better way to figure out the tiebreaker is with a tiebreaker question where the one who answers first is safe.

Or what if there was a randomizer where no one is safe if a tie happens. The latter definitely invites a lot more chaos into Celebrity Weakest Link than there already is, but it would keep me invested and a bit more on the edge of my seat. There are a lot of ways Celebrity Weakest Link could upgrade this stiff moment in the show, but part of me thinks I’m just screaming into a void of network TV.

Aside from my problem with Celebrity Weakest Link, it’s consistently a delight to watch. You can tune into new episodes on Monday nights over on, or enjoy episodes with a Hulu subscription.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

#3753. A former volunteer is threatening legal action against fan-made game project Skyblivion

A former volunteer is threatening legal action against Skyblivion, the long-running fan remake of Oblivion built in Skyrim's engine, over code they contributed to the project.

The unofficial project, which remakes 2006's The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion, is being made by volunteers from the TES Renewal Project, the modding group that also works on Morrowind remake Skywind.

Bethesda has allowed the project to continue on condition that it replaces all of the original game's assets, and the team continued working on it after Bethesda released its own Oblivion Remastered in April 2025.

In a statement posted to Twitter/X on 30th October, the Skyblivion team said that after the volunteer left, the two sides disagreed over the "continued use and maintenance" of their work.

A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG

The main issue was the team's decompilation of parts of that code, which it said was needed "to maintain functionality and fix issues" after its access to the original source code repository was revoked.

According to the team, the volunteer then "escalated to sending legal threats", including demands for the real names and home addresses of its volunteer team leads. The team said this was "something we couldn't accept and think is disproportionate".

The team said it has consulted legal counsel and is "completely confident in our right to maintain the code they submitted". Even so, it said it removed the code "to protect our volunteers from undue stress and ensure a clean break", rebuilding that system from scratch.

Despite this, it says the threats have continued. Its post says the former volunteer is "attempting to sue", but it's not clear whether a lawsuit has actually been filed. The volunteer has not been named.

"Please don't make this a witch-hunt," the team told fans, adding that it wishes the former volunteer "the very best" and hopes to "get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with our planned release of Skyblivion".

Last December, the team delayed Skyblivion from 2025 into 2026.

#3751. Cult PC-98 Zombie Gore Fest Re-Animated On Steam With First Official English Port

To most international players, the PC-88 and PC-98 series of machines are still a trench of undiscovered gems. With thousands of games and an uncanny interface, fan translators have only cracked the surface of this esoteric library. One of its most infamous entries was FairyTaleâs 1992 gross out Dead of the Brain, an adventure game about a zombie outbreak, and the developerâs first foray into horror from the erotica scene. Funnily enough, that seems to be a similar case as the publisher, who brought this lurid classic back to life this weekend.

In Dead of the Brain, Cole and Dr. Cooger seem to have a Doc Brown and Marty thing going on. Unfortunately for Cole, this late night phone call isnât a summons to check out some tricked out DeLorean. Cooger, it seems, has crafted a formula to revive the dead. Initially testing it on his house cat, the suddenly feral animal kills a passing police officer. As the two try to cover their perversions of science, the glowing formula makes the rounds. The streets are quickly overrun with oozing ghouls, but not all is as it appears in this city of the dead. You will have to point, click and shoot your way to uncover a most bizarre conspiracy.

The game takes open inspirations from horror classics like George Romeroâs Living Dead saga and Brian Yuznaâs nasty Re-Animator films. Because of its handcrafted new localization, the tongue-in-cheek approach comes through grinning. Reminiscent of the beloved Return of the Living Dead, its young cast are fully aware of the stereotypes of the story, but have no choice but to reenact it regardless.

Released in 1992, Dead of the Brain was the first plunge into horror from developer FairyTale. It summoned a direct sequel and a spin-off in the ‘Nightmare Collection,’ but prior to it FairyTale’s games were almost exclusively erotica. Funnily enough, this new port has been published by FAKKU, the long-running hentai platform, who have begun a program to bring other retro Japanese, non-pornographic games to modern hardware. On their socials, FAKKU said that they had to lop off a few racier sequences to avoid a harsher rating on Steam, but that fans can unlock them with a free patch available on their homepage. In the near future, FAKKU will also be publishing the madcap 1992 RPG Dengeki Nurse.

Amid a backdrop of AI-spawned language patches, it has been an otherwise stellar year for creepy retro classics brought to modern hardware. On top of Dead of the Brain, this week saw both Ecstatica games remastered on Steam, and earlier in the year the FMV oddity The Dark Eye was made available (albeit under a perplexing new name).

When Mass Effect 3's beloved multiplayer mode was left out of the Legendary Edition, there was much wailing and gnashing of teeth. Redemption has finally come in the form of the ME3Tweaks modding team, who have spent the last three years quietly working to not only get multiplayer working, but improve it.

"It's not just a ME3MP port but rather an extensive remaster of the experience," says modder Audemus. "This includes new features like bringing forward LE's native features like controller support/HDR, overhauled UI, rebaked level lighting, upscaled/redrawn textures, upgraded shaders, improved networking/server replication, extensive bug fixes, new gameplay modes, and a stable format for future mod support and easy installation/compatibility."

They're even adding new game modes, like one called "Unified" that combines enemies from multiple factions, and letting players either join ME3Tweaks' server, or set up their own private servers.

The ME3Tweaks team are the same modders who previously revived and revised the Pinnacle Station expansion, a lost DLC for the original Mass Effect that was also left out of the Legendary Edition. They're planning to release the multiplayer mod on N7 Day, which is also when composer Sam Hulick plans to release a re-scored version of the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer.

#3749. Silent Hill: Townfall adds new Hard difficulty in latest update

Silent Hill: Townfall has added a new Hard difficulty mode and rebalanced every existing setting to make room for it.

The update, patch 1.6.0, went live on PS5, Steam, and the Epic Games Store earlier this week, according to patch notes published by Konami. Konami said the rebalance is designed to create "a smoother difficulty curve for players to choose from".

As part of that rebalance, resources have been adjusted in some sections of the game, and enemies' hearing now gets sharper as the difficulty level goes up. Your position is now visible on the map in whichever mode you pick, while the reduction to the main enemy's attack severity now applies only in Story Mode.

Anyone who picks Nightmare for their first playthrough will now see a warning screen. The difficulty selection menu also gives a clearer summary of how the options differ.

SILENT HILL: TownfallNotice: Game Update (Patch 1.6.0)An update tuning gameplay and addressing some in-game issues is now available.Please check that the version number in the lower right corner of the main menu is displayed as v1.6.155963.*The PlayStation®5 version is…

The update also improves the valve status lighting for colourblind players, adds more hints and tutorials, and tweaks the wording of some puzzle hints and items. The options menu has been reorganised into clearer categories, and the controls remapping option has been renamed to make it clear that keyboard and mouse commands can be remapped there too, not just controllers.

PC players also get a new DLSS Ray Reconstruction option, alongside the usual general improvements and bug fixes.

To check you're on the latest version, look for v1.6.155963 in the lower right corner of the main menu on PC, or v1.6.156035 on PS5.

Developed by Screen Burn and published by Konami, Silent Hill: Townfall launched on PS5 and PC on 24th September. Matt said Townfall showed Silent Hill's "stellar revival continues as new developer Screen Burn melds stealth, meticulous world design, and a dash of social realism for a different sort of survival horror", and awarded it four out of five stars in Eurogamer's Silent Hill: Townfall review.

#3745. Final Fantasy 14 reveals Evercold’s second new job and February release date, with pre-orders opening next week

Plus Square Enix confirms Final Fantasy 14 has passed 35m registered accounts.

Final Fantasy 14's next expansion, Evercold, will launch on 23rd February 2027, and its second new job is zephyr, a physical ranged DPS that fights with a crossbow and a bird.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida revealed the job during the opening keynote of the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo. Zephyr pairs crossbow shots with support from an avian familiar called Nephele, and joins Bastion, the greatshield-wielding tank revealed as Evercold's first new job at Fan Festival Berlin earlier this year.

Pre-orders for Evercold and the previously announced Collector's Box open on Wednesday 4th November at 9am GMT. Anyone who pre-orders gets early access, plus a Wind-Up Köttr minion and Halone's Earring, which boosts EXP from defeating enemies by 30 percent. The in-game items are delivered as soon as you pre-order, so you can use the earring to level jobs before Evercold arrives.

The Collector's Box is physical goods only. It doesn't include the game, in-game items or pre-order bonuses. Inside you'll find an art box featuring an Evercold illustration by Yoshitaka Amano, a figure of the Warrior of Light as a reaper, an Ethos metal keychain, a Köttr mini plush, and a Tapestry of the Fourth.

The Square Enix Store is also selling a limited Collector's Bundle that pairs the box with a code for the Digital Collector's Edition on Windows or Mac. Players on PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, and Steam can buy the box on its own and pre-order the Digital Collector's Edition separately. The digital edition adds a Valhallar Odin mount, an Entreat Crystal emote, and a Crystal Skyltborg weapon for Bastion.

Square Enix also used the keynote to reveal a new Fierce raid difficulty, sitting between Normal and Savage; a new trailer for the Evangelion: Ghosts of Desire alliance raid crossover, plus tougher eight-player battles built around some of its bosses; and new Tetsuya Nomura artwork for Beyond the Lifestream, a raid series crossover with the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series.

We can also expect Evolved Combat Mode, which Square Enix says highlights each job's unique identity; Seasons, a new system that changes how item rewards are earned; and expanded character creation with new Character Action Skins. Expanded housing features, PvP updates, and a revamped companion chocobo system will follow from patch 8.1.

Final Fantasy 14 has passed 35 million registered accounts.

You can watch the full keynote on Twitch, and there's more on the official Evercold site.

Final Fantasy 14 is now available on Switch 2. The port was announced at the end of June.

In a new Q&A vlog on his YouTube channel, Obsidian studio design director Josh Sawyer took a question about why there are so few RPGs in contemporary urban settings. Part of the problem, according to Sawyer: They're more difficult and costly to make than other RPG environments.

"One of the issues as an RPG developer that we've found⁠—at least at Obsidian and Black Isle⁠—is that, compared to a dungeon, generally speaking, a town is four times the expense per square foot, basically. Not really "square foot" but, if you have a map of a given size. If you have a dungeon that's this big, it costs X. If you have a town that's populated with people that feels realistic, that's four times as expensive.

"Obviously, that's a generalization, but that's something that is reflected in our [past] work. As we work on areas over time, when we get towards the end, we realize: 'Holy crap, we spent forever trying to do these maps.'

"For example, at the end of [Pillars of Eternity], we had to do Twin Elms. And that was, one: A big pacing landmine that a lot of people did not appreciate⁠—so, sorry about that. But also, we're back to doing very expensive content. You might ask: 'Well, what's the expense?'

"There's a high density of NPCs, a lot of characters have dialogue. They have their own⁠—maybe not super-unique appearances⁠—but there's just a lot more custom stuff that goes into setting up towns, usually. They're more expensive. Obviously you can do it, though."

Elsewhere in this section, Sawyer cited Baldur's Gate 2's Athkatla, Disco Elysium, and the recent Zero Parades as RPGs that land the plane on believable, dense urban environments⁠—though Sawyer notes that the latter two have the advantage of not needing to work in as many believable combat encounters as other RPGs.

A few others spring to mind for me: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3's version of the titular city. But all of those really highlight Sawyer's point about expense and challenge. Vampire and Cyberpunk were notoriously difficult development cycles for their respective studios. I'll always be a BG3 Act 3 defender, but it's definitely the part of the game with the most noticeable seams.

But even if they're hard to make, I love urban adventures in RPGs, whether as part or the whole of a game. Novigrad and Oxenfurt are two of my favorite parts of The Witcher 3, for example. For a real niche example of an urban RPG you should have on your radar, I highly recommend the early access Moves of the Diamond Hand.

These days, Michael Che is one of the four most seasoned veterans who’ve been on Saturday Night Live (a show that's seen a lot of turnover lately) for over a decade. That means when he does interviews, he’s frequently asked about his long history of seeing a ton of celebs come and go as host. He just gave an excellent reason as to why he’s not keen on getting into the nitty-gritty of the topic.

Che and Colin Jost are back on SNL 52 on the 2026 TV schedule for their 13th season as the hosts of Weekend Update. Here’s what Che had to say about why he chooses not to talk too in-depth about the behind-the-scenes of working with the hosts:

SNL is such a vulnerable place for everybody. Like for us, we work there. We're there all the time. We're comfortable, and people would ask like, ‘Who's the worst and who's the best.’ And I'm like, it's really not fair to say who’s – to judge somebody based on their time there, because they're there for a week.

When Che was on What Now? With Trevor Noah, he gave this candid explanation about what it's like for hosts on SNL. He also likened being on the SNL staff to “planning someone else’s wedding” every week. Since it’s a big deal for anyone who gets asked to host, there’s a lot going on at once, and they aren’t usually at their best. As he added:

It's scary, it's fast. There's no other show like it, so there's no way to prepare for it unless you just do it all the time. So, if you're hosting SNL and you don't trust the table read, you don't think it's funny, you don't trust the rehearsals and the run-throughs and the like, you don't know the process. So, why would you trust [that]?.... Especially if you don't do comedy at all.

Michael Che explained the chaotic week of a host on Saturday Night Live, too. Here’s how it goes. On Monday, the host meets everyone. Tuesday is pitch day, and Wednesday involves a packed eight-hour day of table reads that sometimes include upwards of 40 sketches. Then, on Thursday, they do rewrites, rehearsals and camera blocking. And Friday is when they do the pre-tapes. Before they know it, they’re live on Saturday night! Scary, right?

As the cast member explained, the whole thing becomes normal for everyone who works there, but it’s completely foreign and daunting to anyone coming into the process. He continued:

So, if somebody's showing you something like, ‘Trust me, it's going to work,’ and you don't find it funny, but you got to do it live on television, you're like, ‘You're going to make me look stupid. People going to think I'm not funny.’

It’s a lot of trust the celebrities have to put into everyone at SNL, so I appreciate what Michael Che is saying regarding why he doesn’t judge people on a really weird week of their lives. I wouldn't have thought about this otherwise. Also, in his words:

So, like a lot of times people have a rough go, but it's not because they're bad people. It's just because it's a scary situation.

Clearly, Che enjoys the process himself because he’s continued to come back every season since starting first as a writer in 2013. He and Jost have been consistently good co-hosts on their segment of the show, with their joke swap being a particularly memorable bit between them. The pair also had a hilarious bit outside of SNL when they were on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire this week and deliberated over a NSFW Taylor Swift song. Now, he'll be back in Studio 8H with his colleagues and a new batch of hosts.

While we likely won’t be hearing from Che about what they were like as hosts, next in this season’s lineup are Inde Navarrette, Druski and John Mulaney. You can catch SNL on Saturday nights at 11:30 p.m. ET on NBC or with a Peacock subscription.

#3742. Activision to remove Itaewon crowd crush footage from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and apologises to victims' families

"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims."

Activision has apologised to the bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it will remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

In a new statement reported by Inven Global, Activision said the footage "will be completely removed" via a game update scheduled to roll out on 12th November.

The statement was issued in Korean, and the quotes come via Inven Global's AI-assisted, editor-reviewed translation.

As we reported earlier this week, the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died. The bereaved families' association and the Citizens Countermeasure Meeting called for its removal.

"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims who were deeply hurt by this incident, as well as to everyone we have caused concern," Activision said.

The publisher also said that Modern Warfare 4 "is a work of fiction created to provide realistic immersion", and it "never intended to evoke or trivialise any tragic event, including the Itaewon crowd crush" by using real news broadcast footage.

The controversy has also reached the South Korean government. During a press briefing, minister of the interior and safety Yun Ho-jung described the footage's inclusion as "secondary harm", and said: "I believe appropriate sanctions should be imposed".

"Using such a tragedy as material for a game, a form of entertainment or business, is something that should be refrained from as a matter of human ethics," Yun added. He said it was up to the relevant agencies to decide "whether to impose punishment or block it to make general access difficult".

Activision's earlier statement to Eurogamer said the opening cinematic "utilises some real world news coverage to establish the game's fictional narrative", and was "not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form".

#3741. Valve’s Cancelled Portal Prequel F-Stop Has Leaked

F-Stop, Valveâs cancelled 2007 Portal prequel, has leaked onlineâand yes, itâs fully playable. If youâve heard of F-Stop, you donât need me to tell you why this is a huge deal. But if you havenât, then youâre in for quite the history lesson.

In 2007, Valve spent three months on a project that Gabe Newell would later dub the Directed Design Experiments. Now, Iâm not going to attempt to tell the story better than the folks at the Half-Life wiki have before, so hereâs the short version: during these three months, Valve broke off into five teams. Each team designed and partially created a video game âexperiment,â and the fifth was dubbed âF-Stop.â

F-Stop was conceptualised as a prequel to Portal, and the gameplay revolved around using an experimental Aperture Science camera to mess with perspectives and solve puzzles. Gabe Newell himself was very taken with the project, but playtesters were less thrilled. Ultimately, F-Stop was scrapped, and some of its dialogue, characters, and mechanics were reworked into Portal 2.

Well, consider it scrapped no longer, as thanks to the efforts of several leakers and the Valve Cut Content team, F-Stop is now playable in (almost) its entirety.

If youâre curious as to how this leaked, the long answer is that itâs actually a combination of three separate leaks. Some of you might remember that in late August, roughly 13 terabytes of Steam depot data leaked online. The leak, dubbed Steam2, seemingly contained almost every Steam depot from 2003 to 2013 and, most surprisingly, assets for F-Stop.

However, while the Steam2 leak included the majority of F-Stopâs assets, it did not include F-Stopâs source code or its mapsrc data (Valveâs folder name for its map source code data). It appears both of these final pieces of the F-Stop puzzle were leaked via the Valve Cut Content projectâs Discord server over the past 48 hours.

According to the mods in the server, the person who leaked the F-Stop mapsrc initially asked for $1,000, but, for whatever reason, just ended up giving them away for free anyway. The Valve Cut Content team has verified the map files’ authenticity, and the community has combined all three of the puzzle pieces into the end result: a fully playable version of F-Stop.

Those who have played it are reporting that while there appear to be a few missing assets and dialogue lines here and there, itâs essentially 99 percent complete. Unsurprising, as I’m sure Valve would have added a little more polish if they ever planned to release this officially, but hey, letâs be realââ99 percent completeâ is a hell of a lot more than the 0 percent complete we had this time last week.

#3739. PUBG live-action series in the works at Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct and star

PUBG is being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Krafton announced the adaptation on 30th October, adding that Glover's brother Stephen, his writing partner on Atlanta, will join the project as a writer and executive producer.

The series will also be executive produced by Michael Schaefer for Neon TV, Fam Udeorji for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee for LV3H. LV3H is Krafton's entertainment arm, and it's involved in both developing and producing the show.

There's no word yet on a release window, plot, or who else will star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

Earlier this month, Krafton revealed it was ending development of PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction shooter spin-off announced nearly a year ago. The publisher’s other games include Subnautica and InZoi.

#3737. How to collect map fragment at The $.$. Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters mini-season has introduced all kinds of epic scavenger hunts to tackle around the island. One of these hunts is tied to map fragments, with the very first quest you need to tackle asking you to collect a map fragment at The $.$. Rocky.

Even in a mini-season like this one, the island is still pretty large, which means there are lots of places you have to carefully search to find quest items. It’s a fairly daunting task to take on, so if you’re struggling with this one, here’s how to collect a map fragment at The $.$. Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

You can find the map fragment at The $.$. Rocky near the far southern end of this key POI in Fortnite. Specifically, it’s located in a room found on the lower levels of the large ship docked at this location.

To find the map fragment, land at The $.$. Rocky, which can be found near the middle eastern end of the island. Once you’re there, make your way over to the large grey ship if you didn’t land directly on it.

Head inside the ship, then make your way down to the lower levels. As you’re working on this, you’ll spot a small white diamond icon with an exclamation point in it. This icon marks the precise location of the map fragment found here, so focus on getting closer to it as you descend.

If you’re having trouble finding staircases that lead lower, consider simply breaking the floor beneath you to reach the right spot more quickly. The map fragment can be found sitting near a crate inside a room situated on the lower levels near the southern end of the ship.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Once you find the map fragment located at The $.$. Rocky, walk up to it and hold down the button that appears next to the “Gather the map fragment” text that pops up next to it. As soon as you do, the map fragment will officially be gathered, thus checking off the first step in this larger overarching quest.

In total, there are seven map fragments you must find to fully finish this task. Only one is available to grab each week the season is live, though, so you have to wait and steadily progress to earn them all.

If you’re up for some more exploring and adventuring, there’s plenty more to get done this season. Next, you might consider checking out all Treasure Hunters battle pass skins, trying to access the Pirate Shop, finding Devil Fruits, and solving the Frog Statue puzzle.

Warning! Spoilers ahead for Chicago P.D. Season 14, Episode 4, “My Eye, My Call,” streaming now with a Peacock subscription.

Changes have bene unfolding on Chicago P.D. during its run on the 2026 TV schedule. Original cast member LaRoyce Hawkins officially exited the procedural in Season 14, Episode 2, bringing his time as Officer Kevin Atwater to a close. There was no telling how Intelligence was going to move on after losing yet another member of the team, though it seems the series has already found Atwater's replacement. While I didn’t know what to expect, there is already one thing I love about him.

The recent Chicago P.D. episode “My Eye, My Call” puts a lot of focus on a new officer, Donovan “Penny” Watts, played by Naiqui Macabroad. He's a young beat cop who has been patrolling the 11th District for the last six years. After the murder of an acquaintance, Donovan offers to assist Voight on the investigation, which is connected to an ongoing case.

Donovan soon gets too involved in the case, so much so that he arrives first on scene at a raid on a stash house. Despite Voight telling him to wait for backup, Donovan proceeds, noting that he believes young children are inside. His hunch proves to be right, with a mother and her son being held hostage by two armed criminals. Donovan tries to de-escalate the situation before Intelligence takes action, but one criminal gets shot, while the other is handcuffed.

Donovan's instincts and drive lead Voight to offer him the open position on Intelligence, saying that the Unit is down an officer. With that, Donovan accepts.

While viewers have only Donovan in one episode thus far, he already seems like a good fit for the. Something I really love is that he goes by his instincts. The young man even tells Voight that he’s called Penny because he’s a bad penny -- he sees something, he moves on it. That kind of energy is just what the team needs.

Penny clearly knew the consequences of defying a direct order from Voight and understood the safety risks. Yet he also understood the repercussions of not going right in. Considering Donovan's approach to the job, I'm eager to see how his work with the team progresses this season.

So far, fans have seen how Donovan works, and what he’s willing to do to help someone. However, we have yet to see him work with Intelligence, and that's going to be a whole new ballgame for him. He’s been on the patrol beat for six years, so it’s going to be interesting for him to transition from that to being part of an actual unit (and a famous unit at that). It's hard to watch Chicago P.D. without Hawkins, but Macabroad is already making his mark.

Chicago P.D. Dropped A Heartbreaking Update On Imani And Her Sister In The Season 14 Premiere

Donovan is obviously a good cop who cares, which is why he goes off his instincts. However, sometimes, that’s not a good thing, because it could seriously put someone in harm’s way. I’m hoping that the longer he works with Intelligence, the more he’ll get acclimated to working in a team and working together. The last thing I'd ever want to see is anyone on the team or otherwise getting harmed due to impulsiveness on Penny's part.

Of course, everyone on Intelligence has great instincts, and they will do whatever it takes to save someone, meaning Donovan is in the perfect place. If Voight wasn’t sure about him, he definitely wouldn’t have offered him the spot. Intelligence has seen a lot of cops come and go, but I have a feeling Naiqui Macabroad's Donovan could stick around for quite some time.

Make sure to tune into Season 14 of Chicago P.D. on Wednesdays at 10 p.m. ET on NBC to see how Donovan fits into Intelligence. All episodes are also streaming on Peacock.

#3733. How to get Solid Gold A$AP Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters season is shaping up to be perhaps the most generous season of all time, with loads of free cosmetics up for grabs. One of the rarest and most special items you can get is Solid Gold A$AP Rocky.

Lots of the mechanics featured in this season are unlike anything we’ve seen before, so figuring out how to get your hands on this freebie and others like it can be tricky. To ensure you don’t miss out on this epic prize, here’s how to get Solid Gold A$AP Rocky in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

Solid Gold A$AP Rocky is a random treasure chest loot item, which means there’s a chance you might find him while looting anywhere around the Fortnite island. He is not a guaranteed drop at any point, and is one of the rarest items in rotation, so it generally takes a lot of searching and quite a bit of good luck to acquire him.

Anytime you open a treasure chest, you might only find standard loot, or you may instead also be rewarded with some extra special freebies. Solid Gold A$AP Rocky is one of the potential prizes included among the bonus goodies you may find.

All of the potential bonus assets you may find while looting are as follows.

Since there’s a pretty expansive pool of potential bonus items you might find while looting, actually getting Solid Gold A$AP Rocky can be tough, as many of the other possible items have better drop rates than he does. Still, all you can do is loot as much as possible and hope luck favors you.

You’ll know you’ve found Solid Gold A$AP Rocky or another special item from the bonus pool when you get a gold pop-up near the top middle section of the screen. This pop-up will highlight the prize you found, which is then granted to you upon returning to the lobby after the round ends.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Solid Gold A$AP Rocky can potentially be found in any treasure chest around the island. There are no fixed spawn locations for this loot drop, so anytime you find and open a chest while he’s featured in the loot pool, there’s a chance you may unlock him.

Solid Gold A$AP Rocky is available to find in the loot pool from Nov. 1 to Nov. 7. The featured skin switches over to Lil Uzi Vert at 8am CT on Nov. 7, so you have about a week to search for it before it leaves the pool.

#3732. Dune: Awakening's free Blood and Ice expansion swaps sand for snow on 1st December

Funcom's survival MMO Dune: Awakening is heading north with a free expansion that trades the deserts of Arrakis for a frozen new map.

The expansion, called Blood and Ice, will release on 1st December. Funcom said it adds "around 35 hours of new progression", along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialisation traits. It's coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox.

The new map, called the Polar Sink, turns the game's usual survival loop upside down. Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm, upgrading your gear with resources found only in the Polar Sink.

The map is split into two biomes, the tundra and the ice cap. You'll start in the tundra, where wealthy water shipper families have built lavish strongholds, before trying to get into the heavily guarded ice cap. Once you're in, you can harvest ice to cool your base equipment and speed up production.

According to Funcom, the expansion "brings the focus back to ground-level survival, with traversal, temperature management, and combat all playing important roles in your progression". The studio also said future updates will add more reasons to go back to the region.

Blood and Ice also brings a new Events tab to the main menu. Shortly after the expansion launches, a new event called Water Crisis will follow the current one, The Scourge. Funcom says every event can be completed in both single-player and multiplayer, and that it plans to run them more often, each with new stories and free rewards.

Funcom has also launched a cosmetics store, which it says will help fund continued development and free updates. The store will start with a rotating selection of items, including looks taken from the Dune films to coincide with Dune: Part Three's release in cinemas this December. The plan is to eventually make the full catalogue available at all times.

Several of the community's most-requested features are also on the way. Offline single-player is due this month, and from January 2027 you'll be able to copy characters from multiplayer servers to single-player, and from single-player to select private or self-hosted servers on PC. Full cross-play will also arrive in January 2027.

"We're far from done," Funcom said, adding that it has "ambitious plans for the year ahead", including major free updates in 2027. The studio says more than a million new players have joined since the game launched on consoles, alongside a rebuilt endgame, three DLCs, and the conclusion of the game's first story arc, Book One.

Just a couple of weeks ago, Norwegian developer Funcom, creator of Dune: Awakening and Conan Exiles - and many other games - confirmed it was entering a period of restructuring and bracing for layoffs as a result. You may remember the company making a similar move this time last year, months after the initial PC release of Dune: Awakening.

Avalon Hill's deluxe rerelease of the classic dungeon crawl board game HeroQuest is getting a digital edition courtesy of Nomad Games, who previously adapted board games like Talisman, Love Letter, and Fury of Dracula. Expect goblin-bashing, trap-disarming, treasure-hunting, and spell-casting. I'll use my broadsword.

PlayStation 2skateboardingTony Hawk's Pro SkaterTony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4

Tony Hawk, skateboard legend, video game superstar and the last one to die in the great uprising, has inspired the culture for generations. Since Neversoft put him on the PlayStation in 1999, Hawk has been a household name, the video game series inspiring boarders on the couch and halfpipe alike. Looking to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3, he traveled to the real world Los Angeles park recreated within the game. Only to be escorted out by security.

“Happy 25th THPS3!” Posted the Birdman himself. “We got kicked out of Pershing Square while shooting this today.”

Though unnamed in the game, the Los Angeles stage of Tony Hawkâs Pro Skater 3 is clearly inspired by Pershing Square, a business park in the cityâs financial district. With its distinctive modernist features from architect Ricardo Legorreta, the stone crescent benches and large red orbs made for a slick backdrop in the 2001 extreme sports game. It still remains in the city today, largely unchanged, as well as the nearby car wash with a big blue obelisk.

As such, recreating the beloved video game should have made for easy content. To the Ramones’ Blitzkrieg Bop, Hawk rolls through Pershing Square, revisiting the sights, recreating the worbling idle stance of his virtual avatar. Leaving most of the tricks to his PlayStation self, Hawk and his team could only film so much before being ejected from the site by security.

“She [security] just shooâd us away,” posted Hawk. “It was very anticlimactic.”

The third entry in the series was the first to hit the PlayStation 2. To this day itâs considered not just one of the best in the series, but is tied with Grand Theft Auto 3 as Metacritic’s best on the console. The game was remade in 2025, part of Iron Galaxyâs Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 bundle. While the first set was met with a ticker-tape parade, the secondâs reception was a touch milder. Fans young and old continue to be frustrated as getting new, no nonsense entries in any legacy skateboard series feels like pulling teeth, when they could be losing them off a botched rail grind instead.

#3729. Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online

Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online.

The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake".

Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload. There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style.

Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment.

Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats.

How do you solve a problem like Persona 4? At Gamescom, we sat down with series director Kazuhisa Wada to talk about the Persona 4 Remake, and ask about how Atlus is approaching the original text for the remake.

"We are putting in serious consideration on the sense of tempo."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"This time we are putting in serious consideration on the sense of tempo, back at Dawntrail we were being really careful in depicting new lands, new cultures, new encounters and this greatly slowed down the pacing on story progression. The fact that this did not align with the player's motivation of 'keep moving forward' shows shortcomings on my part as the director.

"For Evercold, segments that focus on above-mentioned elements are moved to side quests, and we made it so that players can enjoy them at their own pace after, and pay our attention to the sense of tempo," via the r/FFXIV subreddit.

As PC Gamer's premier 'I think too much about the story Dawntrail could've been' person (which is a proper, official title, don't look it up), I have some thoughts about this.

Now to be clear, this is a translated quote from a group interview, and while Yoshi-P is certainly involved in the process of writing any expansion, he's a game director, so he's got an overarching view rather than a handle on the nitty-gritty of a given storyline. However, I don't think the issue in Dawntrail was its over-emphasis on worldbuilding, it was a lack of interest in how that worldbuilding connected to character.

Sure, the whole 'talk to three people' questlines get deservedly dunked on as a clumsy vehicle for how this stuff gets conveyed, but I don't really have any problem with how Dawntrail sets up the continent of Tural itself. As a matter of fact, I think the baseline is all very interesting—a fledgling nation under a first king at the end of his life, forced to reckon with how succession will work? That's a fun setup.

The stumbling of Dawntrail is in how none of these worldbuilding details had knock-on effects for the characters in any real, meaningful way. We learn about these cultures, and they either barely come up again or they add little to the core emotional conflicts that the characters are going through, with the exception of the Mamool Ja and the Skydeep Cenote.

Gulool Ja Ja, the warrior-king soon to abdicate the throne, basically does no wrong throughout all the stories we learn of him (aside from his raising of Zoraal Ja, which isn't really explored anyway) giving absolutely nothing for the main cast to reflect on. Wuk Lamat's relationship with her siblings is never meaningfully or memorably explored in the context of the societies she's learning about.

Even the rite of succession messes up clean opportunities—there's a whole segment where contestants are randomly assigned to partners, and rather than use this as an opportunity to have Wuk Lamat, say, paired with someone she doesn't like, she just gets put with Koana and nothing really happens as a result.

Textured worldbuilding isn't the issue—the issue is that worldbuilding should generally feed back into the overarching themes and narrative. I'm not sure simply offloading all of it into the story's sidequests is the answer, rather than having a considered effort to make it interesting and relevant to the characters at hand.

But again, I'm not expecting Yoshi-P to sate my hunger for nitty-gritty nuance through the filter of translation in a group interview—and the current Evercold introductory patch story does give me hope, given there's already been some effective show-not-tell worldbuilding in it. The fact Visna freaks out about us approaching without stating our brand is great, it immediately sets the stakes for life in this ice-covered world without beating us over the head with it. So there is genuine hope that FF14's story really is returning to form.

Wait, Han Solo could have been Spider-Man?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Alden Ehrenreich has had a pretty impressive career, and he's only 36. Between playing a young Han Solo to working with the likes of the Coen Brothers, Christopher Nolan, Woody Allen and Francis Ford Coppola, a lot has gone right for him. However, I just found out he also went up for Spider-Man way back when. This week he recalled his audition story, and why he thinks he “blew” it. All I have to say is: oof!

So often we hear about the success stories of Hollywood, so honestly this is sort of a refreshing story to hear. As Ehrenreich remembers it:

Yes, I went up for I think it's that I went up for the Andrew Garfield Spider-Man…. I remember him coming walking in when I was walking out.

That would have been around 2010, when Ehrenreich had just started his career in Hollywood. From what we’ve heard from the auditions for The Amazing Spider-Man in the past, it featured some stiff competition. Josh Hutcherson was in the mix, along with Logan Lerman reportedly being on the shortlist. Joe Jonas has also talked about auditioning for the movie, too. Ultimately, though, it was Garfield who landed his dream role.

When Ehrenreich shared the audition story with Josh Horowitz, he admitted he didn’t really want to play Peter Parker because of where he was at “internally” at the time. He also said that at the time he was auditioning for it, it seemed to be “the same story” as Tobey Maguire’s version to him. Here’s what he said about the audition itself:

I'm not suggesting that I would have gotten the role. I think Andrew Garfield is one of the best actors in my generation, easily. He's incredible, and I'm sure he would have gotten it anyway. But I showed up woefully unprepared for that in a way that I would never do later. Like, I was 22, I think, or 21, and I kind of showed up not memorized and got there and there was a full set. There was a scene with 10 actors having dinner, and they were off book, and I was not. So if I did have a chance for that, then I think I blew that up.

When the Weapons actor reflects on the audition, he doesn’t sound regretful, though. He pointed out that getting really famous at the age of 22 “would have been a really bad idea.” He has much preferred having a “very gradual” rise to fame instead. As he added:

I think I also felt that it wasn't my role and that it wasn't right for me. I didn't want to do it.

Instead, Ehrenreich went on to do movies like Beautiful Creatures, Blue Jasmine and Hail, Caesar! in his early twenties. 2018’s Solo: A Star Wars Story was the big moment when he became more recognizable, and he was 26 at the time. And he did actually join the MCU for Ironheart last year!

As of late, the actor has been on a winning streak of movies as well. He was in Best Picture winner Oppenheimer, arguably the best horror movie of last year, Weapons, and his new movie now in theaters, A Talent For Murder, has him working with Helen Mirren. Plus, as we look to the future, he’s going to be in Miami Vice ‘85 with Michael B. Jordan, Austin Butler, Danny Ramirez, John Leguizamo, Walton Goggins and Haley Lu Richardson.

While it may look like Alden Ehrenreich missed out by not being prepared for his Spider-Man audition on paper, it sounds like it all worked out as it should, and he’s perhaps even grateful he didn’t get it.

#3725. Team Behind Fan-Made Oblivion Remake Face Lawsuit From Former Contributor

BethesdaFan gameThe Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion RemasteredThe Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

Since 2012, a team of Elder Scrolls fans have been assembling a total conversion of Oblivion to run off the engine of its descendant, Skyrim. Known as “Skyblivion” the fan-project has spent over a decade in development. While a lengthy development is often filled with ups and downs, its latest woe is a rather unique one, as developers say that one of their former members is threatening litigation.

“Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivionâs development departed the project,” posted The Elder Scrolls Renewal Project. “We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure.”

A former volunteer is attempting to sue Skyblivion and we need your help pic.twitter.com/3Ee5eQTELG

— Skyblivion (@TESRSkyblivion) October 30, 2026

According to the statement, an unnamed volunteer contributor left the team a short time ago. Since leaving, there has been a great deal of contention around the work they left behind. The former developer, according to the post, objected to the “decompilation of parts of their work,” something bound to happen as other aspects are reworked and improved. In response, the disgruntled party sent a legal threat, demanding the real names of others involved.

To temper the situation, the statement says they decided to remove the code and contributions in question, but despite that the former member has “continued to intensify their threats.” In a video plea, Kyle Rebel says that one anonymous community member demanding the legal names of the others is unacceptable. In kind, they also ask supporters not to”make this a witch-hunt,” requesting pro-bono legal assistance and resources over any online campaign to sniff out the unnamed troll. The nature of their contributions, the reasons for their departure, and what contractual agreements were made (if any) are left unspecified.

“A “take your ball and go home” approach like this fundamentally contradicts the collaborative, open spirit of the modding community that makes massive passion projects like this possible,” reads the statement. “While weâve consulted with legal counsel and are completely confident in our right to maintain the code they submitted, we had zero interest in holding onto friction or fighting a former team member.”

Skyblivion has become something of a Ship of Theseus. Originally aimed to be a direct port, work generally evolved into something closer to a hide-to-hair remake that would be implemented as a Steam mod. While anonymous, the team of hobby developers is estimated to have grown to around 40 strong. They had aimed for a 2025 release, though by the end of the year they admitted it would need more time. Obviously another hurdle was the release of Bethesdaâs own remastered Oblivion that same year, though the community said it wouldnât stop their efforts.

Fan-projects are no strangers to legal threats, many having to bow out or become entirely new when the official studios rattle their tail. In this case, however, Bethesda was vocally supportive of Skyblivion, and the litigation has come from within.

#3724. How to use Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

In Fortnite Treasure Hunters, there are lots of special, seasonal Sprites waiting to be found around the island. One of the first quests you’ll encounter tasks you with using Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests.

The process for acquiring Sprites changes a bit each season, and this task is quite unlike anything we’ve seen before, so it can be a bit tricky to navigate at first. If you’re struggling to get through it, here’s how to use Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests in Fortnite.

You can find Sprite Wanted Posters hanging up on walls anywhere around the Fortnite island. They’re marked with a special symbol and glow color different from the ones used for chests, which makes locating them a bit easier.

Sprite Wanted Posters are marked with a square, poster-shaped icon that has a question mark on it. The glow for these special posters is a softer, slightly lighter gold shade than the one that marks regular chests.

All Wanted Posters are consumables, which means only one player can find and use each one, as they turn into a Sprite Treasure Map you can use as soon as you interact with them. Because of this, they’re more common earlier on in each round.

#3723. Modern Warfare 4 on Switch 2 has much worse input lag than PS5

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Switch 2 has noticeably worse input lag than on PS5, which could put Nintendo players at a disadvantage in multiplayer.

Digital Foundry's tech review measured multiplayer latency at 81ms when docked and an average of 100ms in portable mode, against 49ms on PS5. Testing used wireless controllers on both consoles (a Switch 2 Pro Controller and a DualSense), and portable results ranged from 83ms at best to 125ms at worst.

Digital Foundry said "responsiveness here simply isn't as good as on other consoles", and described the lag in portable mode as "actually deleterious to performance" (thanks, IGN).

Beyond the lag, Digital Foundry is fairly positive about the port. Multiplayer runs at 60fps most of the time, and if your TV supports VRR, you'll notice the drops less. The campaign is capped at 30fps and resolution is dynamic.

Docked with DLSS on, the game targets 900p, but Digital Foundry saw it drop to 450p in busier scenes, such as the Paris vehicle chase. In portable mode, the target is 720p, with drops to 360p.

It's been 13 years since a Call of Duty game last appeared on Nintendo hardware, with Ghosts on Wii U in 2013. The series' return is the result of a 10-year deal Microsoft offered Nintendo while it sought regulatory approval for its $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard.

Yesterday we reported that Activision has apologised to the bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it will remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Valve's second mighty expensive, yet mighty impressive VR headset, the Steam Frame, launched in the latter half of September, meaning October was the first full month where players could actually use it. The latest Steam Hardware Survey suggests a rather big bump in usage for Valve's VR headset this past month.

In September, the Steam Frame accounted for just 0.41% of VR headset usage. In October, that number jumped to 4.13%. That means it surpassed the Oculus Rift S, Sony PS VR2, HTC Vive, Windows Mixed Reality (which is a platform, as opposed to a single headset), the first Oculus Rift and Bigscreen Beyond. It is now the sixth most popular VR headset, sitting just .37% behind the Pico 4, and a hefty 24.14% behind the Meta Quest 3.

The 3.72% increase for the Steam Frame is the biggest jump upwards in October, and the biggest tumble was taken by the Oculus Quest 2, which lost 3.57%.

The Steam Frame officially released on September 18, with preorders going live on September 14, but that doesn't mean buyers got their hands on the headset on the day it went live. So the bump can not only be partially attributed to continued sales over October, but also to shipping times.

It's also worth noting that both the 256 GB and 1 TB models are backordered, meaning even if you sign up for one now, you will simply be put on a waiting list. That means Frame usage is unlikely to entirely stagnate from here.

Given the Steam Frame has enjoyed such a large bump even with customers struggling to get their hands on the headset, this suggests the VR market on Steam isn't huge. Though it is worth taking these stats with a pinch of salt.

The Steam Hardware Survey is an opt-in survey Valve takes every month. This means it only looks at a fraction of Steam users to get general statistics. This is why stats tend to change a tad each month. For instance, the Nvidia GeForce RTX 3060 is currently the most popular graphics card in the survey, but it saw a 0.08% increase last month. The RTX 4060 saw a downward shift of 0.40%, pushing it below the RTX 3060.

As such, the Hardware Survey can only ever give a rough reading of usage each month, but it still seems like a good sign for Valve's latest bit of hardware.

Last week, it was revealed that Savannah Chrisley married Jason Galanis over the summer and that they were also expecting their first child. Todd later addressed the big news when he appeared alongside Julie on Bunnie Xo’s Dumb Blonde podcast (which is shared on YouTube). The Chrisley patriarch had nothing but kind words to share about Galanis, going as far as to call him “brilliant.” With that, Todd also mentioned another point about why the the relationship is apparently so beneficial for his daughter:

He didn't care about the show business, because this man is brilliant. He’s brilliant, and [Savannah] is emotionally set for life, but she’s financially set for life…. She was good on her own but not like she is today.

A businessman, Galanis most notably worked with Hunter Biden and the latter’s associate, Devon Archer. In September 2020, Galanis was sentenced to 189 months in prison due to his reported involvement in several offenses related to securities fraud. Historically, Todd has been quite protective of his daughter, with his comments about her co-hosting The View alone proving that notion. All the while, questions still remain in regard to Julie and Todd Chrisley’s money matters, especially in the wake of documents having surfaced. The Chrisleys reportedly still owe $1,571,452, per a tax lien filed by the IRS in August 2026. Said filing consists of two assessments, with one of those including an unpaid balance of $142,410.72 for the tax period ending in Dec. 31, 2021. As for the second assessment, it mentions a total of $1,429,041.89 that’s unpaid for the period ending with December 31, 2022.

The Chrisleys’ financial portfolio was also at the center of their 2022 trial, which ended with them being found guilty of bank fraud, tax evasion and more and sentenced to years in prison. Julie was initially set to serve seven years behind bars, while Todd was to serve 12. Per the verdict, the Chrisley Knows Best stars were ordered to pay 17.2 million in restitution, and it was alleged that they’d have to sell assets to cover the bill. As of this writing, that debt has reportedly not been paid due to the couple’s appeals.

Even though not much is known about the specifics of Todd and Julie Chrisley’s money, the couple divulged that they paid around $3 million in legal fees amid their court battle. As for any financial issues, Todd has been coy about his net worth at this time. It remains to be seen if the couple will address their reported tax issues and if Savannah Chrisley chooses to say anything about her dad’s claim about her own financial standing.

#3720. Patrick Stewart, Our Captain Of Multimedia CD-ROM Edutainment

In 1997, Patrick Stewart took me on a voyage through the stars from the comfort of the family computer room. An interactive expansion of a 1993 video cassette, Nine Worlds allowed you to travel the solar system, pick up gift shop postcards, scientific and cultural history of each neighboring planet, all accompanied by bombastic (and slightly compressed) renditions of Gustav Holstâs famous celestial suites. And of course, with the guided audio tour from Stewart himself, whose impassioned chronology of Mars only netted me a C+ on my homework.

“To the Romans and Greeks, it was the god of war,” orates computer Stewart, “to others IT WAS THE RED EYE OF THE DEVIL HIMSELF!”

In the days since his shocking passing, fans have found themselves with so much to parse from the multifaceted thespian. Of course, to most, he was the eloquent, insightful Captain Jean-Luc Picard, whose fascinations of the cosmos led the crew on Star Trek: The Next Generation. To others he was the fatherly Professor X across the sprawling X-Men films. He was also a master of stagecraft, an outspoken advocate, a baker of erotic cakes, and a Beavis and Butt-Head superfan.

To those of a certain age, he was also an educator. Or, more specifically, an edutainer. Following Mystâs bank-making showcase of what CD-ROMs were capable of, classrooms and home computers experienced a surge of educational software. There had long existed Math Blasters and illustrious typing teachers, but with the assistance of compressed video and tinny audio, publishers sought to bring the classroom experience home.

While most celebrities needed to be charged on a DUI to edutain, the Next Gen crew seemed eager to moonlight as teachers. Of course, LeVar Burton had long hosted Reading Rainbow by the time he donned La Forgeâs visor, setting some precedent. While Riker was elsewhere teaching celebrity poker, Patrick Stewart captained numerous suites of multimedia CD-ROMs.

"Now go, explore, and enjoy. The adventure is yours."

— âï¸Beth âï¸ (@rollinrabbit.bsky.social) 2026-10-29T20:27:45.134Z

Sure, narrating a cultural history of our solar system makes sense given his resume, but Stewart was also recruited to guide young users in Compton’s Interactive Encyclopedia, a literary play-by-play of the Titanicâs final hours, among many other loose discs. His outstanding voice, powerful but kind, made him an ideal messenger for worldly information. It was an era where people were still learning how to use these machines, never mind learn from them. And in this brief era of scholarly CD, Stewart passed on the fascinations exhibited by his most famed performances.

While it didnât do me a ton of good on my immediate school work, many of these pieces of software imparted some deeply rooted pieces of information, continuing to rattle around my skull. As someone who would later on adore passing out to Carl Sagan, I didnât fully appreciate the psychic history of the Red Planet offered by Stewart. But the amount of context and culture squished into a meager disc is a fascination of its own. Where and how kids learn from computers going forward might be dubious, but there was an era of enthusiasm to reimagining games and education. When we aspired to reach higher, Stewart found himself a star there too.

#3719. At Dead of Night sequel The Great Hugo is coming "(very) soon"

Baggy Cat Games, the team behind viral FMV horror game At Dead Of Night, has confirmed that a sequel is "coming (very) soon".

At Dead Of Night 2: The Great Hugo picks up where the original game left off and reunites us with Maya as she heads off to investigate a large Tudor manor house.

At Dead Of Night became famous quickly during the pandemic thanks to streamers and content creators like Markiplier, 8-BitRyan, John Wolfe, and DomPlays, who introduced us to Jimmy Hall, a creepy hotel landlord hellbent on recruiting an audience for his late-night comedy show and psychopathic comedy alter ego, Hugo Punch.

The new game, subtitled The Great Hugo, picks up half a decade later.

"Five years later, Maya is still haunted by her experiences in Sea View Hotel," the blurb teases. "Desperate for answers she remembers the ghost box she used in the hotel, left there when she escaped.

"After searching on [auction] sites and in antique shops, she finds a similar looking device, but can’t get it to work. She contacts an old friend and counsellor, Quinn, who had helped her understand her supernatural experiences in the hotel. Quinn recognises the device and knows where they were made - by an inventor who used to live in a large Tudor manor house not far from Sea View - but warns her against trying to get it working. However, Maya ignores his advice and goes on her own investigation."

Quite how long "(very) soon" is, we don't yet know, but we'll keep you posted.
