"A lot of the sounds in the game are quite unique."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"We bought a wonderful sample library from a piano in Chernobyl that someone had found in the Forbidden Zone. Someone went there and made a sample library from that old piano. So we bought that one and used it," via Arc Raiders' YouTube channel.

Arc Raiders has a terrific soundscape, although it can sometimes be hard to hear it when you're getting hunted down by your fellow players or bloodthirsty arcs. The game is quite quiet, aside from the occasional sound of distant gunfire, the clicks and cracks from small roaming arcs, and the noise of shuffling scrap as raiders sort through abandoned buildings for valuable items. But perhaps the best noise in all of Arc Raiders comes from the few instruments raiders can find amid the rubble.

"One of the gameplay designers, really early on, made a trumpet," Pajor says. "And it was so out of place, and we were like 'why are we making it?'" The musical items in Arc Raiders serve multiple purposes. There's the social incentive to play an instrument, to bond with strangers and just show them that you're a harmless, relatively chill dude. But there's also the strategic purpose of using noises to lure arcs. Perhaps you're herding them into a trap or ambush or maybe you're trying to distract the aggro of one arc away from another vulnerable player.

Avid players of Arc Raiders will notice, however, that there's no trumpet available in game. Well that's because the trumpet eventually became what we now know as the lure grenade. Apparently a playable trumpet was just too silly to the devs at first, so they settled on something a bit more useful. But now, over a year later from launch players can enjoy multiple instruments like the piano, guitar, harmonica, flute, banjo, recorder, and the trusty shaker.

"It's been almost seven years of exploring this world. [Composers Patrik Andrén and Johan Söderqvist] used to be performing musicians before they became composers so they have a lot of friends who are Sweden's best jazz musicians," Pajor adds. "So a lot of the sounds in the game are quite unique because they are making the sound libraries.

"It's their commitment to building a world; they're phenomenal world builders. So eager to understand what the game is and what the world is. They are also very demanding to work with, because they have so many ideas."

Aside from the Chernobyl piano, which is certainly one of the stranger sources of music I've heard of, composers Andrén and Söderqvist are also known for their abstract use of everyday items to make music and noises.

A lot of raw synthesisers are used to create arc-adjacent noises, but they've also hooked up different kinds of fruits to a synthesiser to grab some slightly weirder sounds. All in all, out of a three hour recording session there's usually only three minutes of usable sounds, "because it's sheer weirdness" but those three minutes "are really really really cool", Söderqvist adds, and stresses that you simply can't obtain these fantastically strange sounds another way.

#3715. How to collect map fragments in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

At every turn, Fortnite Treasure Hunters challenges you to embark on all kinds of tricky scavenger hunts. Just about every mission and every item you can find around the island involves some kind of treasure hunt, as is the case with the collect map fragments quest.

This is one of the most difficult tasks you’ll face, as it requires a lot of time, effort, and careful searching to get it done. It does grant a pretty special prize for completion, though, so here’s how to collect map fragments in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.

To complete the collect map fragments quest in Fortnite, you need to carefully scour the island to find and collect six map fragments. This quest is a bit of a tough one to get done, as it’s an overarching goal for the entire mini-season rather than a task you can get done right away.

Each week, a new map fragment will be added to the island. Because of this, you cannot complete this mission all at once, and instead need to work on it over time as the season progresses.

Throughout the season, a fresh map fragment will arrive as each new section of the Adventure tab is unlocked. These fragments correspond to the arrival of additional special characters around the island, like Lil Uzi Vert, A$AP Rocky, and Cap’n Hatsune Miku.

Since you need to collect a total of six map fragments, this mission takes a full six weeks to get done. You can check the Adventure section under the Treasure tab on the home page to see which part of this quest is live.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Each of the six map fragments can only be found at one specific location around the Fortnite island. All of them are only available to collect after their initial unlock date has arrived, so you have to wait to collect them all.

Here’s when each map fragment unlocks and a breakdown of where to find each one. Some details have been revealed for map fragments ahead of their arrival, while others are entirely unknown. We’ll update all details here as they become available to help you obtain them all.

Fully finishing the collect map fragments quest unlocks the X Marks The Zero Point Sliver Loading Screen as a reward. This is a completely free reward that’s automatically granted once you’ve successfully gathered all six map fragments. You also get 10,000 XP for each piece you find.

While you wait for more map fragments to unlock, there are lots of other missions to keep you busy around the island. Some good ones to work on are using Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests, unlocking all Treasure Hunters battle pass skins, and solving the Frog Statue puzzle.

#3714. Phantom Blade Zero is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, selling over 4 million copies in three days

Phantom Blade Zero studio S-Game has announced that its debut title has sold more than 4m copies in its first 72 hours on sale. The game's official X account broke the news alongside a celebratory message, though without providing a per-platform breakdown of copies sold.

"Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!" the developer wrote on X.

Phantom Blade Zero is available on Steam and PlayStation 5, but the 4m figure also includes sales made on the China-exclusive Tencent WeGame PC launcher. Prior to launch, Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott estimated Phantom Blade Zero to have sold over 1m copies before it had even released.

It was always clear the third-person character action game was going to be a hit, we just had to wait for actual figures to be released.

Phantom Blade Zero attracted over 431,000 concurrent players on Steam at launch, a figure that kept risking and rising into the weekend, ultimately settling at a massive 833,921 peak concurrent (via SteamDB). Just in case it wasn't already clear, this is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, beating the likes of Forza Horizon 6 and far outpacing all other major releases such as Onimusha: Way of the Sword, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Ace Combat 8.

Despite the very strong opening weekend's numbers, Phantom Blade Zero has not been able to match or exceed the performance of Black Myth: Wukong, 2024's also-Chinese developed triple-A action game, just yet. The breakout hit, estimated to have sold 30m copies since, is one of Steam's largest debuts ever, peaking at 2,415,714 concurrent players at launch.

In Eurogamer's Phantom Blade Zero review, Emma Kent spoke highly of much of the game, but was critical of its underwhelming narrative and lack of consistency, writing: "This game is exceptional in so many areas - the animations, the beautiful environments - and when the combat works, the sense of flow is incredible. Then you walk into a boss battle and feel all that power fade, like you're waiting your turn to get hits in with a wooden sword."

Potentially getting much more out of existing hardware is nothing to sniff at.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While I go 'oo' at every perfectly lit videogame vista, ray tracing can sometimes make my gaming rig go 'HNNNG'. I love a traced ray as much as the next person, but realistic reflections and lighting can be a bit of a memory hog. Thankfully, Microsoft is previewing something new for DirectX that could significantly take the load off many ageing rigs.

It's a pair of features called 'Clustered Geometry' and 'Partitioned TLAS'. At the risk of oversimplifying, you can think of this DirectX update as bringing tech very similar to Nvidia RTX Mega Geometry to every other GPU vendor.

Obviously there's more to it than that, though, with Microsoft describing this as the "most significant update [to DXR] since its debut in 2018." Top line: Microsoft's own testing of this update suggests it could reduce ray tracing memory load by as much as 90% without the need for a team green GPU (via Techspot).

So, how does it work? Well, without this update, ray tracing is already beaming between less detailed versions of the geometry you see in-game. Traditional ray tracing tech does this because bouncing around detailed models afresh for every frame would simply take too long.

Clustered geometry slices up the detailed models into neat little packages of 256 triangles or fewer. Partitioned TLAS then does a similar thing for the entire videogame vista, splitting a scene into smaller regions. Why? Well, rather than searching the entire map every time, looking for what's changed and updating the frame accordingly, the ol' dread pirate Ray Tracing needs only to run their finger over the quadrants they know are different, marking the spot with 'X'—or something like that, the metaphor got away from me a bit in the middle there.

Basically, this fresh DirectX tech massively simplifies the ray tracing data your rig has to check and update frame to frame. That could free up a whole lotta memory, with Microsoft demonstrating a reduction of 7.5 GB to 774 MB on an AMD Radeon RX 9070. Obviously, frame rates also benefitted, jumping from a wince-worthy 1.2 fps to a very impressive 79 fps in Microsoft's testing.

Now, this isn't really a case of simply installing an update and, 'whee, you're flying!' Microsoft issues a fair few caveats—for one thing, not all games are going to replicate the wins its specialised test environment saw.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

For another, working with clustered geometry and all of those packages of up to 256 triangles uses a lot more temporary scratch memory compared to traditional tech—that presents its own logistical concerns for game developers.

It's also worth reiterating that this update is not yet widely available, and there's no word yet on when PC gamers like you and me will be able to get our mitts on it either. If you feel like going sicko mode, though, Microsoft writes you can gain access to experimental features like this by using "matching Agility SDK preview headers and runtime, a supporting driver, and Windows Developer Mode."

Still, the potential to cut down memory usage without needing to buy any new hardware is very promising during these times of runaway pricing for both memory and GPUs. If I can put off a pricey upgrade for a few years more, I'll be happy.

Scream is my favorite horror movie of all time.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Halloween is this weekend, so plenty of folks will be re-watching the best horror movies to celebrate. My personal favorite of all time is Wes Craven's original Scream, which is streaming with a Paramount+ subscription and started one of the best horror franchises ever. I recently made my Gen Z friend watch it for the first time, and his reactions really cracked me up.

I'm currently in full spooky season mode, recently attending a Rocky Horror shadow cast. Afterward, my friend and I went back to my place, where I peer-pressured him into watching Scream for the first time. I thought the movie was basically monoculture, but he was delightfully clueless.

When I say my friend didn't know anything about Scream, I mean it. Not even those scenes that have pierced pop culture forever came across his desk, allowing him to have a fresh, unfiltered take when I pressed play. That includes Drew Barrymore's opening scene and the plot twist of her being the first victim. Just like the original audiences from the '90s, he was absolutely shocked when Casey was brutally killed by Ghostface before the movie's title even hit the screen.

He was also surprised by some of the other cast members that popped up throughout the movie's 111-minute runtime. He was shocked to see Courteney Cox as Gal Weathers, even though she is the only actor to appear in every single movie in the franchise. Despite the long career she's had, he was shocked to see Monica from Friends in an R-rated horror flick.

Another huge twist that got the best of my friend was the reveal that Ghostface was actually two different people: Matthew Lillard's Stu Macher and Skeet Ulrich's Billy Loomis. He agreed by the end that the two characters were gay-coded, but he was as shocked as Sidney at the reveal that two people had been under the killer's mask the whole time.

Given how much Scream had been parodied over the years, I assumed that even the most casual moviegoer would be spoiled on the movie's twists and turns. But some of the zoomers out there missed the memo, like my dear friend. So he got to watch the movie unbiased in a way I never got to. Despite it coming out in 1996, he was impressed with the dialogue and performances. What's more, he was taken by how the lack of cell phones raised the stakes of the film.

In many ways, it felt like my Zoomer friend responded to the same things that shook '90s audiences when Scream first hit theaters. I loved seeing these parallels, and thought this proved yet again why Wes Craven's slasher flick continues to be so timeless decades later.

The entire Scream franchise is streaming now on Paramount+, including the seventh movie that arrived earlier this year as part of the 2026 movie release list. Now I just have to convince my friend to watch the sequels and rate them. Hey, a guy can dream.

#3711. Easiest way to get the Pirate Token Shop in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

The Treasure Hunters mini-season has sent all Fortnite players on a wild hunt, as the Pirate Shop has several premium items for you to redeem at zero cost. Typically, you’ll need to spend V-Bucks to buy these items, but you can get all of this for free for a limited period of time. It depends on you accessing the Pirate Token Shop first.

To raise your chances, you will have to open as many regular chests as possible during your adventures. You can, however, accelerate the process with a few simple tricks.

To get the tokens, you have to open as many chests as possible. That’s the only way to obtain it. However, here’s how you can strategize the whole process.

First, you have to drop on the map and look in areas that have higher concentration of these chests. If you visit a spot that has limited number of chests, chances are that someone else might have opened them and received the rewards. More chests provide you with more opportunities at finding the tokens.

Next, you’ll want to get the Plundarggh Sprite. This sprite increases you movement speed whenever you open a chest. This fits nicely into our loop since we will open as many chests as possible. Doing so will increase your speed, and this allows you to save time while traveling between different chests.

Finally, you’ll want to play in squad fill if you don’t have friends. All members of party will get the access tokens if one you get it from the chest. Hence, playing in a party makes complete sense since you can open thrice the number of chests in a round that you might be able to do alone.

Ultimately, it will boil down to your luck when it comes to unlocking the Pirate Shop. Once done, you’ll have 14 days to redeem all the available rewards and applicable cosmetics.

#3710. Soulframe to launch into free open beta this week, as Warframe devs go head-to-head with WoW: Forever

Soulframe's Preludes (its own version of a beta) is finally opening its doors to the whole world ahead of the Verse of the Veilands update. Starting this week, anyone who wants to can simply download the game and hop in, no invite required.

The date this happens is an interesting one: 6th November. That's two days after the release of World of Warcraft: Forever and the same week as Old School RuneScape's Hardcore worlds, so it's suddenly become a pretty packed month for MMO enthusiasts.

This comes after three years of closed testing for the fantasy action MMORPG, which players have been able to gradually see firsthand through sporadic invites. With Soulframe suffering delays since its first reveal, brief invite events have already occurred over this period. Even locked away, the game has received multiple substantial updates over the years, including new quests, Pacts (classes), factions and so on.

As for what newcomers to Soulframe can look forward to when Soulframe opens its doors, the Verse of the Veillands update is bringing a total overhaul of the map progression system this month. After the completion of an early quest, players are introduced to a corrupted landscape, the Veillands, which they must purify.

As you do so, new resources will be obtainable and side activities like fishing will be unlocked. You'll also be able to train up a small wolf pet into a full-on mount in the process. Previously, players were just thrust into the open world to explore and figure things out as they go, so this should provide something of an introduction to the game's open map. It won't be totally finished when released mind you, with updates to the Veillands system coming in the future.

On top of that, there's a new Pact called the Ode Shrike coming with the update. It's a tricksy trapper with spikes, balloon snares, bombs and chains to disrupt enemies as you whittle them down.

Could this be enough to win people over to Digital Extreme's newest project? Time will tell - but in the meantime its long-lasting sci-fi MMO Warframe is taking players to the Tau system in a major next step in the game's narrative this December. It comes with a detective noir inspired main quest, playable warframe, and even an in-universe Poker equivalent.

Bobby Moynihan was back on SNL last night, and he's still got it.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The big talking point from Saturday Night Live’s Halloween episode is, of course, Tom Hanks’ surprise cameo. The A-lister and beloved member of the five-timers club reprised his role as David S Pumpkins during last night’s cold open to the delight of the crowd. I was obviously stoked to see Hanks too, but since everyone else is giving him his shine, I need to spend a few paragraphs talking about the other SNL cameo we got during Inde Navarrette’s episode.

If the skeletons behind Hanks’ David S Pumpkins seemed familiar, it’s because current cast member Mikey Day and longtime former cast member Bobby Moynihan have played the sassy dancing skeletons (who both have amazing names) in the other David S Pumpkins sketches too. The two co-created the sketch alongside Streeter Seidell and have played supporting roles in each version.

It’s obviously not a surprise to see Day back for last night’s version, but it was a welcome surprise to see Moynihan back too. He clearly has a great relationship with everyone at 30 Rock and has returned several times to make appearances since, but given he’s a working actor currently starring in Fall & Rise Of Reggie Dinkins, you never know. You can watch Hanks, Moynihan and Day do their thing in the latest David S Pumpkins sketch below…

I would have been happy just seeing Moynihan return as the skeleton, but to the delight of myself and many other fans, he actually made a second appearance on SNL last night too. He showed up on Weekend Update to give us another round of Drunk Uncle. It turns out the character is just as enjoyable as ever, as he gave us updated takes on pitch challenges in baseball, Mrs. Met and hot gay hockey shows.

He also introduced the Milwaukee Brewers, who recently won the World Series, the first in the team’s history. Christian Yelich, Brice Turang and manager Pat Murphy all made cameo appearances and interacted a bit with Drunk Uncle. Amusingly, Moynihan referred to Yelich as Pete Davidson, which continued a theme of referring to Colin Jost as former cast members including Seth Meyers and Amy Poehler. You can watch the whole Drunk Uncle appearance below…

People often measure different SNL eras based on their most successful cast members, but the truth is the success or failure of SNL is often directly related to how good the key supports are. Moynihan is a great example of that. He was never the most famous performer during his nine seasons on the show, but he was always a key guy who could elevate a few sketches each week and be entrusted to carry one of his own. He’s a key reason why the 2010s were so good, even if he’s not quite as famous of a name as Andy Samberg, Kristen Wiig, Bill Hader or Jason Sudeikis.

I have no idea if we’ll see any fun cameos in the coming weeks, but I do know we should be in for some banger SNL episodes with amazing upcoming hosts. Next week we’re getting guest host Druski, and he’ll be followed by stand-up comedian and longtime writer John Mulaney. Both of those episodes have the potential to be top tier. I can’t wait.

#3707. "We're doing great," says id Software boss, despite losing "about half of our studio" amid devastating Xbox cuts

Iconic Doom and Quake developer id Software was among the most heavily impacted Microsoft-owned studios during Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's devastating business "reset" earlier this year, with around 136 employees reportedly losing their jobs.

In the wake of those layoffs, id Software co-studio director Marty Stratton was recently asked about the current state of the developer, and how it has been affected by Sharma's cuts. "We're doing great," Stratton told journalists at a recent event (via IGN).

"Not to handwave the [layoffs] away… everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that," he continued. "But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department."

This is not the first time a senior id Software member has pushed back on the narrative the studio has been "nerfed into the ground and gutted". Hugo Martin, id's other co-studio head previously claimed the remaining team is "the size we were when we made Doom 2016, and id Tech is very much alive and well".

Sharma's Xbox reset will ultimately see 3,200 jobs cut across Microsoft's gaming division, with many of those still to come. Those impacted by the first wave of cuts in July, however, included developers working on the id Software's id Tech engine. This is the engine behind all of the studio's games, and is known to be among the most performant engines, consistently producing visually-impressive games that require modest specs to run.

Following the layoffs, many inside and outside the studio said the id Tech team had been gutted. Longtime id Software programmer Chris Hays, who notably wasn't among those let go, said at the time, "It is hard to make a game that is triple-A, that is like we've done before, with half the people. And by hard I mean impossible". Hays also claimed "entire departments" and "entire disciplines" are gone.

While Stratton hasn't addressed those comments directly, he revealed id Software is now "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the modern Wolfenstein games, and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. "We've always had a very close partnership with [MachineGames], but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]," he explained.

"We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead."

Id Software's next project remains unclear. MachineGames, on the other hand, recently said it's not done with Wolfenstein, so it's possible a sequel to 2017's The New Colossus is in the works.

#3706. Best Roblox song IDs

There’s just something about listening to your favorite music in a public setting and forcing it upon the ears of others. Roblox has turned this real-world nuisance into a series of games on its platform.

Using a database of uploaded songs, players can input Song IDs to blast their song of choice directly into the ears of strangers all over the world. Here are some of the best.

Prior to a change in March 2022, users could upload virtually any audio file and have it be playable in any game that supported the boombox via a Song ID. The change retroactively made any audio longer than six seconds private. This meant that if you weren’t the person who had originally uploaded the audio file, you would no longer be able to play or hear the sound.

This means the vast majority of Song ID repositories are now functionally useless, and users have been restricted to a much smaller selection of songs and sound clips of varying quality. One important thing to know is that there’s no guarantee that any individual Song ID may work, as they can be made private by either Roblox staff or the user who uploaded it.

Below are 30 absolute bangers to entertain yourself and possibly others around you. I have personally confirmed that each is working at the time of this writing. Go forth, aspiring DJs!

To search for music codes on Roblox, follow these steps:

You’ll discover many sections on the Audio page, from the top Roblox Song IDs to the newest hits of the day. After you find a song, you can get its ID through ‘More Info.’ Discover the correct number from your URL. For instance, mine came out to ‘create.roblox.com/store/asset/75793628822368/Mirage-Portal.’ Thus, the bolded numbers would be utilized as the Song ID.

Playing music in Roblox varies in each game, as they all have different methods. Sometimes, it can cost money with Robux, while other times, it doesn’t cost a thing. To play music for free, play Catalog Heaven, a game that allows you to customize your avatar and battle nearby bases. Once you start playing, select ‘Catalog’ and type in Boombox. There will be a few choices here, including the Boombox Gear 3.0 and Golden Super Fly Boombox. Choose one of them to trigger a prompt to enter Roblox music codes.

Tap on the Boombox again if you want to change songs. You can also stop the music by unequipping it in your inventory. Besides Catalog Heaven, you can see if other games permit music. I discovered that Jailbreak features a Car Stereo mechanic, costing 200 Robux. With this title, you can type in ‘R’ or tap the radio on the bottom-right corner of the screen. Then, enter any Song ID you prefer to listen to some tunes on Jailbreak.

For the most part, it seems like Roblox titles that use music codes require a subscription pass. Therefore, if you’re unsure whether your game is compatible, check the title’s Subscription & Passes section to see if there’s a radio or stereo feature.

Only Roblox game developers can create custom music playlists. It’s associated with a tool used in scripting to create soundtracks for various worlds. If you’re a player, you must manually enter each ID to make your own version of a playlist.

The Punished, coming soon to the outstanding deckbuilder, draw their power from self-flagellation.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Their aesthetic? Chains, whips; spiked. Their mood? Afflicted, condemned, ritualistic. Their angels? Dark. Their maiden? Iron.

Friendship ended with dwarven gearsmiths; my new favorite clan in Monster Train 2 is the tortured edgelords.

The final faction being added to Monster Train 2, The Punished, arrive November 10 as a paid DLC. Their theme is self-damage, with new keywords and spells that, primarily, reward power in exchange for hurting yourself. Your pain? Enemies' bane.

Though existing MT2 clans like the Melting Remnant revolve around forms of sacrifice, The Punished are absolutely thirsty for it. They bring new keywords like Chained (enemy units take half the damage that your units take) that make damage an active solution to enemy waves. The self-flagellation angle likewise brings new purpose to some existing spells and equipment, and jives great with partner clans that provide protection from pain (Lazarus League) or more ways to inflict it (Pyreborne).

Damaging my own guys sounds like a risk-reward tactic that requires sophisticated play. In my first run as The Punished, I anticipated having to do brain-wracking calculus about how much damage to absorb. But instead, I've found the new clan to be one of the most powerful and, at least with one of their champions, easy to play.

A lot of that is down to the utility of their new gimmick, a big purple gem called the Monolith. Here's a breakdown of what makes it special:

"Level up the Monolith by sacrificing cards to earn Devotion, which grants Zeal, which buffs attack and HP for all units" kind of sounds like a line from a ProZD deckbuilder parody video (I will take any opportunity to reference the legendary Dairy Cow combo), but it's really not complicated. Click the purple crystal, make cards go away, permascale a little bit.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Though it can change the calculus for a few units, Zeal isn't that game-breaking on its own: usually you're just increasing the ceiling of a unit's HP to set up cards like Zealot's Halo, an equipment that gives +1 attack for every 1 HP you're missing.

More potent is The Punished's starter champion, Archus, an S-tier champ that amps damage based on lost HP, but has the versatility to debuff enemy damage as well. All of his build paths grant him Flight. His best variant deploys a "Darkshard" into the lane he flies into, a 0-attack artifact that does one of the following, on your choice:

Bloodshed is really, really powerful with the right unit pairings and a cheap spell or two that hurts yourself. What's wild is that Archus can deploy a Darkshard in every lane, with a cooldown of 2 on his flight ability. I might anticipate a nerf on that. Scaling your whole floor from received hits (including self-targeted spells!) is a wonderful way to accelerate sweepers or backline bruisers. Archus good.

Zariel, the other champ, is more advanced. The first angel cast out of heaven, "Zariel has been imprisoned for so long that her original crime has been forgotten to time." Sick. Although, you'd think that that would enable some kind of clemency?

Since her arms and wings are bound in chains, Zariel has no base attack. What she does have are three diverse paths that all play off sponging up as much damage as possible:

I asked Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke what combos the studio has found useful with Zariel. "A lot of Hellhorned cards like Branding Rite, Dark Deal, and Inferno work really well with Zariel's Pain and Chain paths. Pox is a great spell for consistent friendly damage, because it applies Decay 10 to all units," says Cooke. "Zariel's Pain Maiden path especially synergizes well with The Condemned, because the unit has Tenacious, it won't die to any friendly damage and it even amplifies the damage it takes and redirects it to an enemy, so it's great for pinging and stacking Pain while still killing enemies."

On my second run with Zariel, in the final rounds of a battle, I was dealing 1000 damage from her Paintouch ability, and I was doing it each turn because the ability has a cooldown of 1. On a couple other attempts, I couldn't create damage outputting units to pair with her quickly enough, and my run collapsed.

The superstar of the roster might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner.

This is one of the few weaknesses of The Punished—although several units have good base attack, instantaneous damage can be hard to acquire. Reaper of Suffering, The Punished's only sweeper, starts with a generous 60 attack (as much as Demon Fiend, a 4-cost Hellhorned unit), but it also starts Suppressed (meaning she cannot attack), needing a cooldown of 4 to expire before she emerges from that state. Taking damage decreases that cooldown, and incredibly, she heals to full HP when she emerges from Supressed and gains flight when you cross that threshold.

This isn't the only star unit on The Punished. Forsaken Berserker gains one multistrike for every two Monolith levels. Scarred Justicar, an uncommon, ended up being my damage solution on several runs. He simply gains +15 attack when hit by a friendly spell or ability, and considering one of the starter cards deals a gentle 2 damage, you can gain perhaps +30 or +45 attack in a round between spells and other effects. Slap a stack of multistrike and the new 3-cost equipment Sineater on him (Deal 8 damage to self, attack immediately, cooldown 2), and you have a high damage solution that just takes a little time to set up.

The superstar of the roster, though, might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner if you're able to draft it early. This stoic statue unit cannot be healed, but it gains +1 HP on revenge, astoundingly rare health permascaling that is set-and-forget simple. I found myself taking the "enemies gain multistrike" trial just to welcome more attacks against Penitent Sentinel. In some runs I was ending with nearly 300 HP, linked to a Titanite upgrade that effectively doubled that. Wild.

After 12 wins with The Punished, I love that they have several viable units to pick from, and how much they synergize with a variety of clans. I kept finding new ways of winning with Zariel, and my strangest victory was with this configuration:

I had no plan and was mostly freestyling through this, my upgrade selections weren't particularly strong. I was surprised to beat Savagery, let alone the Titans.

After 500 hours in Monster Train 2, it's refreshing to beat the game in an unexpected way. I truly thought this run was doomed because I had little traditional damage, no sweep, no tank, and no decapitating spells.

The Punished's masochistic theme works. And Shiny Shoe's treatment of these tortured angels is nice (their Carolina Panthers-blue skin helps them stand out, even among the pale blue Melting Remnant), though their stoic reverence doesn't leave a lot of room for quirk.

I would've loved to have seen a silly torture sicko among the roster, but I'll settle for Lasher, the first backline unit that hits any friendly units positioned in front of him for 1 damage (I don't recommend relying on Damage Shield when he's on the floor). Just think of it as giving your guys a helpful, spiked-chain pat on the back.

It's appropriate for the final update to a game I like a lot to hurt a little. But Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke did indicate that the studio may not be done with the franchise. "At this time The Punished is the last DLC planned for MT2," Cooke told me. "However, we love the world of Monster Train, and hope to work on more Monster Train games in the future!"

#3704. Google’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Egg Makes The Search Engine What It Always Should’ve Been

GoogleThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Google’s cashing in on the nostalgia reawakened by the Ocarina of Time remake. If you type “zelda” into the Google search bar, you’ll get a glowing, hovering Master Sword in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. Click it, and the browser transports you and the search engine back in time to 1998, when everything was good and nothing hurt, or at least when it wasn’t an absolute pain in the ass to try to find something via Google.

The Google page is bedecked in its old livery: the bygone logo with the exclamation mark, along with old blue links in Times New Roman-ish font and listed, blessedly, in order of importance and relevance. No AI search results, no pesky shopping links, no ads. It’s a big ol’ beacon reminding you of a time when the web held the promise of unlimited information at your fingertips, and wasn’t yet the enshittified, barely ethical infomercial it has become. All for a little “Zelda” joke.

It’s not just “zelda” that’ll get you the nostalgia easter egg. “Ocarina of Time” will get you there too. It’s actually quite funny that Google’s reminding us now of the time when it didn’t suck. Last week, Google lost $475 billion in stock market value, the company’s worst-performing day on the stock market ever, with analysts noting that it had missed its ad revenue targets. The reason: Its own AI search product was eating into that ad revenue. Maybe Google should make the Zelda easter egg last a little longer.

When I think about the challenges that might come with filming sex scenes, the inherent awkwardness of acting out intimacy and wearing very little to no clothes come to mind. However, one of the primary hurdles Wicker dealt with had to do with…well…wicker. That became clear when the man behind the wicker, Alexander Skarsgård, spoke about what it was like shooting sex scenes for this project on the 2026 movie schedule.

As Olivia Colman described, her Wicker co-star, Skarsgård, was “wearing a basket” throughout the making of this film, and that made him less mobile. During an interview with EW, the beloved Wicker Husband actor explained how that restriction informed the intimate sequences they were filming:

The restriction of the costume would inform the sex scenes a little bit because again, we shot those scenes very early on. It was the first couple of days. So I was still figuring out the physicality and what the limitations were of wearing the suit. So there were certain things like in bed, you’re not super nimble, so it’s like, all right, maybe that didn’t quite work. Let’s do it this way instead, and then you figure out a way to make it work.

No matter the circumstances, I’d imagine it’d be hard to get accustomed to performing while covered in wicker. The idea of shooting sex scenes becomes challenging too, because it sounds like the wicker totally changed how Skarsgård was able to move. So, as he and Colman worked through them, he was also figuring out how exactly he could move as the Wicker Husband.

However, it all worked out. The reviews about how horny Wicker is prove that. The chemistry between the two actors proves that too, as Colman noted that while she was embarrassed to be filming such intimate scenes, she also fully trusted Skarsgård, the directors, and the intimacy coordinator. And ultimately, the moments were “so much fun” to film.

Now, as when it comes to the wicker Skarsgård was working with (and yes, you do see all his wicker in this movie), it was designed by Wētā Workshop, and it took him about two hours in the makeup chair to get it on each day. According to him, it was constructed in a very specific way too:

It was made with a combination of organic materials and synthetic, and they had to weave it in a specific way considering how muscles and body parts would move.

I would imagine that, like the Wicker Husband, Skarsgård didn’t give anyone splinters with his costume. However, there’s no denying that there was a learning curve and some challenges when it came to moving around in all that wicker (and yes, that does include the movement required for his intimate scenes with the Fisherwoman).

Overall, Alexander Skarsgård did such a great job as the Wicker Husband, and it was very easy to fall head over heels for him. If you’d like to see him covered in wicker and falling for a Fisherwoman, you can catch Wicker in theaters now.

#3702. Over a decade later, Bloodborne remains so popular it reportedly sold a quarter of a million copies this year alone

Bloodborne, FromSoftware's singular Lovecraftian action-RPG, has reportedly sold more than 251,000 copies this year alone.

That's according to Alinea Analytics head of market analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed the figure in a post on X, noting this brings Bloodborne's total sales up to an estimated 10.4m copies, generating $317m (around £236m) in revenue. Elliot also claimed more than half a million people played Bloodborne in October through PlayStation Plus.

Additionally, 12 percent of those are said to have played Elden Ring during the month, while 6 percent played Dark Souls 3, and 5 percent played Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. There's a cohort of gamers who are always bouncing between different From[Software] games," Elliott pointed out. "Can't blame them, especially with this one."

Bloodborne is a PlayStation exclusive that sadly never left the PS4, despite consistent calls from fans for ports and remasters. While the game is playable on PS5 through backwards compatibility, Bloodborne barely benefits from the console's advanced hardware, only seeing smoother frame pacing. In other words, it's the same game with barely any perceptible upgrades.

Before Sony closed down Demon's Souls remake developer Bluepoint Games earlier this year, the studio reportedly pitched a Bloodborne remake, but original developer FromSoftware didn't want it to happen. When news of the pitch came to light, former Sony Interactive Entertainment Shuhei Yoshida said Bloodborne has a special place in director Hidetaka Miyazaki's heart and speculated the reason it hasn't had a remake is because Miyazaki would prefer to do it himself but doesn't have the time.

"Miyazaki-san really, really loved Bloodborne, what he created," Yoshida said at the time. "So I think he is interested but he's so successful and he's so busy, so he cannot do it himself, and he doesn't want anyone else to touch it."

#3701. As the controversy around AI-created video game copies continues, Anthropic seemingly restricts Claude's cloning abilities

An update to Anthropic's Claude AI software has seemingly blocked the creation of outright clones or copies of existing games. Instead, Claude has been altered to only create "original" games.

Among the first to share news of the change was X user Chasm, who posted a screenshot showing the new rule, purportedly added around 27th October. "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets," it reads. "Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.”.

While Anthropic is yet to issue an official statement on the new rule, technical staff member Addy Osmani commented beneath Chasm's post, confirming the change's legitimacy. He noted it was included because "using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy", but added that creating original games and those built with a user's own assets should still be possible.

Following the new rule's inclusion, users on GitHub shared newfound barriers they'd run into as a result. Reports included being blocked from creating digital modules for board games, and from recreating a commercially produced board game for personal use. Eurogamer has contacted Anthropic for comment on the rule change and its stance on AI game copies.

The modifications to Claude have appeared at a time when AI copies of games have drawn increasing ire, with game communities pushing back against them and developers pulling public-facing demos in fear of having their work stolen. AI-assisted copies of triple-A games have also emerged, including a version of Mario Kart 8 playable in an internet browser. However, this was taken down in a matter of days, presumably thanks to a legal notice from Nintendo.

Of course, even if Claude is prevented from making game copies, other AI tools, such as Deepseek, still lack similar restrictions. Until such measures are ubiquitous, the issue will continue. Given Claude's position as one of the most popular commercial AI tools out there, however, this will certainly make a dent in the problem.

To me, that makes for fantastic TV, and it really helps that Ben Ahlers' character is just so gosh darn likable. Unlike basically every other character in this show, I want him to succeed and find great wealth.

So, in Season 4, I really hope we get to see all the ways his life changes as he gets used to being rich. I loved seeing him downstairs and working in the house. And the juxtaposition of that past with his new reality is fascinating. Plus, we really haven’t watched someone fully rise from rags to riches on this show, and that feels like a storyline that should be prominent in Season 4.

It also feels like Jack really has the potential to shake things up, because he sees the world much differently than the other wealthy folk. Between him being a fresh set of eyes and his connections to the people who still work downstairs, I cannot wait to see how his new standing impacts everyone.

One of my favorite moments in Gilded Age history was when Ada became richer than Agnes, and therefore, the woman of the house.

Of course, this was a massive topic during Season 3, and it caused Ada and Agnes’ power dynamic to totally shift. Seeing them, and specifically Agnes, reckon with that was so dramatic. Now, I want more. I really want to see Cynthia Nixon’s character stand her ground even more, and I want her to make some bold choices with the money she’s inherited.

It seems like it’ll happen too, as Season 4’s trailer shows Agnes saying she needs more money for a dinner, and Ada explaining that she doesn’t want to spend it on that. Of course, Agnes had a comeback for her sister, saying no, but I want Ada to clap back too. It’s time she stopped being bossed around by her sister.

The Gilded Age has had some ridiculous plot twists that I did not see coming. However, I don’t think anything will ever top how unexpected the death of Oscar’s lover, John Adams, was. He was hit by a carriage, and both it and this plot point came out of nowhere.

That happened in Episode 6, and as Oscar dealt with that, he proposed that he marry Enid in Season 3’s finale. Enid, notably, used to be a lady’s maid for Bertha; she got fired for attempting to seduce George, and then she married an older man. When her husband died, Blake Ritson's character proposed they marry so they could join forces and cause chaos while also living the lives they want to live.

All this is to say, they both cause and live for the drama, and I want them to do even more of that in Season 4.

So, with that all laid out, to see if these characters play a bigger role in Season 4, you can catch the premiere of this HBO show that got the world talking on Sunday, November 1 at 9 p.m. ET on HBO or with an HBO Max subscription.

#3698. Will King Charles Be the Last Windsor to Lead the Commonwealth?

According to a report by The Times, King Charles is reportedly aware that he may be the last member of the British royal family to serve as head of the Commonwealth. The reason? His son William, the future monarch of England, reportedly has no intention of succeeding him in this role as well. A prospect that, if confirmed, would mark a significant change in relations between the British monarchy and the organization that brings together 56 countries. For while it is true that William is destined to inherit the throne, it is by no means certain that he wishes to retain every responsibility and tradition associated with the Crown. (Buckingham Palace declined to comment on the Times report to Vanity Fair.)

The issue, in reality, is more complex than it might seem. Unlike the British throne, in fact, the leadership of the Commonwealth is not automatically passed from a sovereign to their heir. It is a symbolic role, and succession is decided by the leaders of the member states. Charles assumed the role after the death of his mother, Elizabeth, but his appointment had been agreed upon by the Commonwealth heads of government in 2018. William, therefore, would not be obligated to accept it.

According to The Times’ report, the Prince of Wales has indicated that he does not wish to become head of the organization when he ascends to the throne. However, this is neither an official announcement from Kensington Palace nor a decision that has already been formalized. To understand the significance of this potential decision, we must look back to Elizabeth. During her 70-year reign, the monarch made the Commonwealth one of the pillars of her institutional work, guiding the transformation of an organization tied to the history of the British Empire into a voluntary association of independent states.

Charles has embraced that legacy with conviction. His commitment to the Commonwealth is an important part of his diplomatic vision and the relationship he intends to maintain with countries united by a shared—and often complex—history. And it is precisely this complexity that makes the current moment particularly delicate. The king is, in fact, preparing for a trip to the Caribbean, scheduled for October 27 through November 4, that will include stops in the Bahamas, Guyana, and Antigua and Barbuda.

This visit comes as the debate over Britain’s colonial past, slavery, and calls for economic reparations continues to take center stage in relations between London and several Caribbean nations.

For some time now, however, Prince William has been associated with the idea of a more streamlined monarchy, with a smaller number of members engaged in official duties and a greater focus on the causes he considers priorities, from the environment to mental health. In this context, a potential relinquishment of the leadership of the Commonwealth could be interpreted as a further sign of change. This does not necessarily mean distancing himself from member countries, but rather a different interpretation of the role the British monarch should play in relation to them.

After all, the Commonwealth does not consist solely of territories that recognize Charles as head of state. It also includes numerous republics, and his leadership does not entail governing powers over member countries. William’s potential selection would therefore raise a primarily symbolic question: Who could represent the organization after Charles, and what relationship would they wish to maintain with the monarchy?

For Charles, who is deeply attached to the Crown’s international role and to continuity with his mother’s reign, the prospect of being the last Windsor to lead the Commonwealth would hold historical significance. For William, on the other hand, it could represent a way to distinguish the constitutional responsibilities of the future sovereign from those belonging to a particular phase of British history.

For now, this is merely a scenario, not a succession that has already been decided. But the question raised by The Times goes beyond an institutional role: It concerns how the British monarchy intends to redefine its presence in the world. The future King William will certainly inherit a crown. But it may be precisely what he chooses not to inherit that best reflects the monarchy to come.

Marvel got a bit of publicity, thanks to SNL.

Saturday Night Live returned this weekend and welcomed another host for Season 52. This time, it was Inde Navarrette – the breakout star of the hit horror film, Obsession – who took to the stage at Studio 8H. While the night was filled with memorable moments Navarette got the ball rolling early on when she referenced Shane Gillis controversial gym clothes comment from his SNL monologue a few weeks ago. Navarrette used Marvel as a way to tee up her quip, and I’m sure the studio is delighted to be pulled into such a wild situation.

Gillis returned to SNL for his third hosting gig on October 10 and caused quite a stir due to his monologue (which is on YouTube). A large portion of the comic’s opening set was focused on his attempts to lose weight and his experience returning to the gym as a result. After talking about crossing paths with “the hottest gay guys you’ve ever seen” while at the gym, Gillis spoke about something that seemingly shocked him in regard to his encounters with women:

Also, I haven't been to the gym in so long. I didn't know women just dressed like whores now. Look, I'm sorry, there's no other way to describe... Have you seen it? I've seen it. The shorts. Have you seen the shorts?

The Tires star – who also dropped an F-bomb during a sketch that night – went on to discuss the shorts, which he described as being “neon” and “artificial, bait-colored.” Gillis then advised that he’s “not allowed” to look at the women dressed in that way since people are “filming” social media videos while at the gym.

Ultimately, Shane Gillis received considerable blowback for his “whore” remarks from various corners of the internet, with celebrities like Dan Levy and SNL alum Ego Nwodim expressing disapproval. Weekend Update co-anchor Michael Che responded to the Gillis controversy, musing that while promoting his new Netflix special, he’d be bombarded with questions on the matter. In time, Che was indeed asked about Gillis while doing press, and he did not seem happy. Also, Che later questioned why he did so many interviews after the fallout.

Navarrette covered more than a few different topics, including her acclaimed (and meme-ified) role as Nikki in Obsession. In time, she also referenced the fact that she’d been cast in one of the biggest upcoming Marvel movies, X-Men. As can be seen on YouTube, it was when she began gushing about her inclusion that she made the reference to Gillis’ comments:

I can't believe I'm saying this, but I'm gonna be in a Marvel movie. And I know it's really important for Marvel that you get really fit. So I've been working out a lot. So, every morning, I put on my little whore outfit, and I hit the gym.

This certainly is the perfect time for Marvel to be referenced in relation to such a messy matter. I mean, the studio only has one of the most highly anticipated movies of the year – Avengers: Doomsday – on the docket and wouldn’t want anything to detract from that. So this joke is certainly well-timed for the brand. (Just so we’re clear, you all can sense my sarcasm, right?) In all seriousness, Marvel Studios more than likely isn’t giving Navarrette’s joke too much thought.

Navarrette obviously wasn’t trying to tie the Disney-owned studio to the Shane Gillis controversy. From a comedy standpoint, her role as Rogue in the X-Men reboot just seemed to serve as an opening for her to nod at Shane Gillis. I obviously can’t speak to exactly how Kevin Feige and co. feel about this SNL quip from one of their latest talent signees. However, I’m definitely not expecting any kind of frustration from execs as a result of this barb.

Check out Inde Navarrette’s episode in its entirety by streaming it with a Peacock subscription. Also, know that Saturday Night Live returns with another new episode next weekend at 11:30 p.m. ET on NBC and will welcome Druski as host and The Strokes as musical guest.

#3696. Photographer Gordon Parks’s Best Shots, From Ingrid Bergman to Muhammad Ali

Everything looks good in the art dealer Jack Shainman’s Tribeca gallery, located in the banking hall of the former New York Life Insurance Company building—complete with a freestanding marble bank vault, which has been sitting in the same landmarked space since the end of the 19th century. Each time Shainman conceives a show for the gallery—appearing around the Corinthian columns, beneath the marble wainscoting—he wants to make sure it’s something unprecedented.

Since 2018, Shainman has collaborated with the Gordon Parks Foundation, an organization dedicated to preserving the work of the New York legend who shot some of the most iconic images of the Civil Rights Era. The gallerist wanted to make his first Gordon Parks show in the marble former banking hall special—different from the last four solo Parks shows he’d put together in his Chelsea spaces.

“With Gordon, every time that I do it, I like to do it differently,” Shainman told me.

Ondria Tanner and Her Grandmother Window-shopping, Mobile, Alabama, 1956.

It was a brisk afternoon a few weeks after “Gordon Parks: Voices in the Mirror” opened, and he was walking me through the galleries, which will be full of iconic Parks photographs up through the first week of November.

“I did two shows back-to-back where we showed the fashion and all the unexpected things that people never knew that Gordon did,” Shainman said. “And then we flipped it to all the iconic images of the March on Washington. So it was really fun to show people that. I’m always combing through, looking for images that you didn’t know about. It’s harder to do than you think.”

For his fifth show of Parks images, Shainman asked a number of luminaries—those who worked with Parks, knew Parks, or posed for Parks—to contribute written texts on the great photographer. Ava DuVernay, who was a publicist for Parks’s 2000 documentary, Half Past Autumn, wrote one. So did two women close to his greatest muses: Lonnie Ali, Muhammad Ali’s widow, and Qubilah Shabazz, the daughter of Malcolm X.

Anderson Cooper also contributed a remembrance. I thought perhaps he participated due to his status as a well-known art collector, but he also has a more personal connection to Parks: His mother, the railroad heiress Gloria Vanderbilt, had a decades-long romantic relationship with the photographer. (It was nonmonogamous for at least some of the time, and they were open about being open.)

“He’s really cool with it, because he says how Gordon was such a ladies’ man,” said Shainman, speaking about Cooper. “I respect Anderson so much for just what he does, let alone that his mother was freaking Gloria Vanderbilt. We know him. He’s an amazing person.”

We walked by Parks’s images of the March on Washington, Malcolm X, Rosa Parks. There were incredible images of a small town, kids playing outside a small grocery store—images that have inspired younger artists such as Tyler Mitchell and Kendrick Lamar, who made an entire music video drawing from Gordon Parks photos.

Boy with June Bug, Fort Scott, Kansas, 1963.

There was also one of Parks’s iconic photos of Ingrid Bergman, shot on the island of Stromboli in 1949. At the time, Bergman had caused an international scandal by leaving her husband and small child for the director helming her upcoming picture, Roberto Rossellini. Rossellini was highly suspicious of all press and kicked most media members off the island while shooting his film, which was also called Stromboli. But at Bergman’s insistence, he let Parks stay, and the photographer captured images of the couple together.

As we walked past the images, Shainman mentioned to me that one of the three children Bergman had with Rossellini is the actor and filmmaker Isabella Rossellini.

“Gordon Parks’s photos of my parents were not affected by the gossip and scandal that swelled around them. My parents had fallen in love with each other before obtaining divorces. They were banned from the United States,” the younger Rossellini wrote in her exhibition contribution. “But Gordon Parks kept a firm eye on them as artists. With one photo alone he could capture the whole intent of their film Stromboli, that is, the cultural clashes that ravaged Italy after World War II. Parks had an incredible ability to synthesize complex realities in a single image.”

Whoopi Goldberg on the Set of The Color Purple, Anson County, North Carolina, 1985.

#3694. I Tried the 'Normatec Go' Compression Boots, and My Calves Have Never Felt Better

We're highlighting the small changes—from useful new gadgets, to fresh productivity techniques, to efficient hacks—that are improving our lives on a weekly basis.

If you've ever been on your feet all day and your calves felt like two sandbags, you know how tough it can be to find relief. I'm a marathon runner, so I know it well. Training blocks mean high mileage, and calves take a beating on every mile. I've tried foam rollers, massage guns, stretching, and my favorite maneuver: lying with my legs up against the wall.

This week's upgrade is the first recovery tool that seems to do all the work for me, and hey—after a long run, I'm not complaining. It's my first foray into compression boots: the Hyperice Normatec Go.

The Normatec Go is a pair of wearable compression sleeves that wrap around your calves and give you a dynamic air compression massage. Hyperice describes it as a fully portable version of its Normatec line, which pro athletes and recovery rooms have used for years.

The sleeves inflate and deflate in a pulsing pattern (as opposed to just squeezing constantly). Hyperice calls this compression "gapless": There are three overlapping zones of 360-degree compression working through the calf. In theory, the wave of pressure helps push fluid and blood through your lower legs, which is why Hyperice says the massage increases circulation and reduces tension and swelling.

Hyperice also points out that the calf is often called the body's "second heart" because it helps push blood back up from your lower legs. That matches my experience: After a long run, calves are where the heaviness and tightness show up first.

The biggest upgrade over traditional compression boots is that you don't need to set up a whole system. You strap on the sleeves, open the app, pick an intensity, and relax. I've worn them at my desk, on the couch, and while answering emails after a long run. I show up to my next run feeling fresher, and for a marathon runner, that's the whole point of recovery.

A few features make the experience better:

Seven compression levels (40 to 200 mmHg), so you can go gentle after an easy run or firm after a long one

The two sleeves always stay in sync for a symmetrical massage

Bluetooth control through the Hyperice app, so you adjust everything from your phone

1.2 pounds total, and TSA friendly, so they can travel with you

Hyperice recommends sessions of about 20 to 30 minutes. You can go up to 60 after a tough workout, or use a shorter 15- to 20-minute session at medium intensity before a run to warm up your legs.

The Normatec Go costs $379. Full-size compression boots that cover your whole leg usually run well over $1,000, so that's a big difference. These only cover the calves, but if calves are where you need relief, you don't have to pay for coverage you won't use. They're also FSA/HSA eligible.

At the same time, the obvious limitation is that these are for calves only. I suppose it's a testament to the product that I've never been more tempted to spring for full-size boots, so that my quads and hamstrings can experience the same treatment.

The battery life also leaves something to be desired. Hyperice claims they last three hours per charge, but in my experience, you're better off charging between every hour or so of use.

If you're training for a race, spending long days on your feet, or just tired of tight, heavy calves, the Normatec Go is the upgrade I'd recommend. I can't imagine my recovery routine without it now.

#3693. GTA 6’s Landmass Is Nearly As Big As GTA 4, GTA 5, And Red Dead Redemption 2 Combined

GTA 6 has a big map, but just how big? According to Rockstar, the GTA 6 map is roughly twice the size of GTA 5's and three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2's. The total landmass in GTA 6, however, is nearly as big as the playable maps for GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined, the developer told Edge magazine.

GTA 6 is a large game in terms of its map and playable areas, but it's also dense, Rockstar says. Co-studio head Aaron Garbut said the game features an "order of magnitude more interiors" than any previous Rockstar game.

"Every back alley is as densely detailed and interesting as the others. You can go anywhere, any random location, and so many people have thought about that location," he said, adding that there are places in GTA 6 that he himself has not personally seen yet, despite working on the game for years.

Also in the interview, Garbut talked about the pressure to deliver with GTA 6. After all, fans have been waiting 13 years and are expecting a lot.

"We can't just trot out something that's what people might expect, or that was the easy thing to do," he said. "We've not compromised on the scale, the detail, the interactivity, the story, the open world. I feel like we've built a pyramid on Everest."

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is absolutely massive, and that makes sense given what Rockstar is saying about the size of the map. Additionally, GTA 6 Online could release in 2027.

Carrying on the tradition of SNL hosts laughing on live TV.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Obsession’s Inde Navarrette made her SNL hosting debut this week, and it proved to be quite an eventful episode (which even included nod at the Shane Gillis/gym clothes conflict). As host Navarrette had to contend with the brutal work schedule, quick costume changes and other elements that come with hosting. Another challenge of being on the show, of course, is not breaking during a performance. And Navarrette learned that, thanks to a Paw Patrol sketch that ended up doing her in.

Normally, Paw Patrol centers on a bunch of adorable animals solving mundane “crimes” around their small town. Saturday Night Live, however, decided to take things a step further for their comedy sketch by combining the hit series with Law and Order: SVU and having the pups on solve grisly crimes. It’s a funny concept, and Navarrette apparently found it hilarious, given she completely broke character while she was describing one of the gang crimes. You can see the full sketch below:

While series creator Lorne Michaels famously doesn’t like when the cast or host breaks character, it happens all the time, so Navarrette is in good company. Bill Hader famously broke constantly while serving as a cast member on SNL, and so did Jimmy Fallon. Ryan Gosling is also notorious for breaking during sketches like Beavis and Butt-Head and for absolutely losing it during the Alien Encounter sketch.

Some of the most famous moments on the long-running sketch comedy series have actually come from a host breaking. A perfect example was when Lindsay Lohan couldn’t keep it together during a Debbie Downer segment.

The reason Michaels doesn’t love breaking is because it makes the audience laugh at the actor laughing, rather than the sketch itself. In some respects, that can be seen as kind of be a cheap way to get the audience to laugh if a sketch is bombing. However, breaking still is part of a long SNL tradition, with some of the all-time breaks becoming more iconic than the sketch itself. Also, there’s a reason it’s a surefire way to get a laugh, people love to laugh when other people do, and it’s truly infectious.

Tom Hanks Wasn’t The Only Surprise Cameo On Last Night’s SNL

Of course, Navarrette’s laugh was completely authentic, and she clearly wasn’t desperate to save a sketch or make an audience happy. She was just absolutely tickled by the ridiculousness of the Paw Patrol sketch and some of the hilariously innocent phrases she was using when talking about a dark murder.

The Superman & Lois alum also recovered well and was able to carry on with the sketch and keep it together for the rest of the comedy bit, which is no easy feat. All in all, it seems like a successful outing from a first-time host, and I think she has earned an invitation to do it again when the time comes.

You can check out Inde Navarrette’s Saturday Night Live hosting debut, as well as the rest of the episodes from this season, now with a Peacock subscription. Additionally, you can see her make her breakthrough in Obsession, which is also streaming on the platform. Fans of the NBC mainstay should also check out the show next week, where Internet sensation Druski is hosting with musical guest The Strokes amid the 2026 TV schedule.

#3691. Xbox CEO Says Xbox Series X|S Is Supply Constrained, But Is It?

In the US, you can buy an Xbox Series X|S at Best Buy, Target, Walmart, and even on Xbox's own website. But Xbox CEO Asha Sharma claimed on X that "console sales remain constrained by supply" while discussing revenue decline for her division in the most recent financial quarter for Microsoft. 

To be clear, Sharma doesn't state in what markets or regions there are supply problems for Xbox Series X|S. Here's specifically what she stated on social media:

"In Q1, Xbox revenue declined 2% [year over year], compared with a 10% decline a quarter ago, while our accountability margin improved. Minecraft and WoW Forever set records, Call of Duty had its most acclaimed release in more than a decade, and our PC platform revenue grew double digits. Console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available. We're working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program."

In June, Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball also argued there was a supply-side issue with Xbox Series X|S. "We are producing them as quickly as possible," Ball said at the time. "These is a severe limitation to how quickly we can do that, but it’s not a question of appetite."

Circana senior director Mat Piscatella expressed skepticism about Sharma's console-supply argument on Bluesky, noting that "the data I've seen do not suggest that stock has been the biggest driver of Xbox hardware performance." In addition, Xbox Series X|S hardware sales continue to crater in the US, setting new record lows for Microsoft's gaming brand. This comes on top of Xbox increasing the cost of consoles again in August. 

From a wider perspective, these financial results come in the midst of Sharma's "reset" of the Xbox business. This initiative has resulted in the loss of roughly 1,600 jobs at Xbox, with more planned in the months ahead; projected studio closures like Ninja Theory and others going independent like Double Fine; as well as Halo now falling under the Activision umbrella.

Earlier this week, Sharma touted the success of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's launch. The FPS series has now made "$40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue." For more, check out GameSpot's Modern Warfare 4 review. 

The past few days have also seen the exit of Xbox's first-ever chief operating officer. Helen Chiang is no longer with the company after being promoted to the position by Sharma just a few months ago.

#3690. GTA 6 Makes A Familiar Open-World Gaming Feature Work In Its Own Way

One feature Grand Theft Auto 6 borrows from modern-day open-world games is the ability to call a ride whenever you need it, but in true Rockstar fashion, it comes with a bit of real-life friction. It's not quite as simple as hitting a button to "even the odds" when you need to make a fast getaway.

As GamesRadar's GTA 6 cover story details, you'll have the option to summon your car via a smartphone app. It won't magically appear, as the Scooter Bros. app will see a company employee drop your vehicle off at your location--for a small fee, of course. Just like the car drop-off services you'll find in real life, these couriers have a compact scooter stashed in the trunk of your car, and they'll ride off into the sunset once they've done their job.

Just don't expect to have time to make a call if you're in the middle of a robbery; you'll need to plan ahead and make sure you have a getaway vehicle nearby. While you can steal a car off a street, it brings a new set of complications. You might run into a driver ready to fight back, the car might have a tracker inside, and it might also be low on fuel.

If you're worried you'll have to refuel often, Rockstar Games described this facet of GTA 6 as a quick diversion, and cars can run for a long time before you need to top up the fuel tank with a fresh supply of go-go juice.

But if you're planning to embark on a life of crime in the game, it looks like there will be several things to account for as Rockstar aims to make GTA 6 an immersive entry in the series with multiple systems in play.

Ahead of its release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, the marketing for GTA 6 has kicked up a gear as more details on the game come to light. We've also learned that the GTA 6 landmass is nearly as big as the playable maps in GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined, the download size is appropriately huge, and a new episode of South Park showed off a new system for being crappy toward your fellow NPCs.
